types.name: cw_net_session
types.doc:
── sessions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Players are slots. Every peer announces its slot and the game's protocol
id in a handshake; a peer with another protocol, or a slot already taken,
is refused (logged). Messages carry a type: 0..31 are the engine's,
32..255 the game's. RELIABLE messages arrive exactly once, in order;
UNRELIABLE ones may be lost or reordered (sequence them yourself if order
matters). Messages are queued and leave in packets on cw_net_flush (or at
the end of cw_net_poll); acks ride on every packet and a keepalive goes
out every 0.1 s, so RTT and loss are measured continuously.
types.decl: typedef struct cw_net_session cw_net_session;

types.name: cw_net_channel
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_NET_RELIABLE = 0, CW_NET_UNRELIABLE = 1 } cw_net_channel;

types.name: cw_net_session_desc
cw_net_peer_stats
cw_net_msg_fn
types.doc:
One handler per message type (a later call replaces it; NULL removes it).
data is valid during the call only.
types.decl: typedef void (*cw_net_msg_fn)(cw_net_session *s, int from, const uint8_t *data, int len, void *user);

types.name: cw_net_peer_fn
types.doc: Peer joined / left listeners (up to 8; adding the same fn + user twice is one).
types.decl: typedef void (*cw_net_peer_fn)(cw_net_session *s, int player, bool connected, void *user);

types.name: cw_rpc_mode
types.doc:
RPC: a node method (cw_node_type_add_method) callable from other peers.
Only configured methods are callable remotely. AUTHORITY: only the node's
authority may call it; ANY_PEER: anyone. call_local: cw_net_rpc also runs
it here.
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_RPC_AUTHORITY, CW_RPC_ANY_PEER } cw_rpc_mode;

types.name: cw_state
types.doc:
── tree snapshots ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Save: every node (type, name, parent, child index), every writable
reflected property of every node (except Node.name, which is structure),
the tree's tick and random state.
Load: frees nodes the snapshot does not have, recreates (by type) nodes it
has and the tree lost, restores order, names and properties (a property is
written only when it differs, so an unchanged tree costs reads only). Node
identity is the node uid; node-valued properties are remapped. Must not be
called while the tree is processing. The hash covers types, structure and
values (not uids, names or pointers): equal on every host for equal state.
types.decl: typedef struct cw_state cw_state;

types.name: cw_state_save_fn
types.doc:
Private (unreflected) state a type keeps: save writes at most cap bytes
and returns the count; load gets them back.
types.decl: typedef int (*cw_state_save_fn)(cw_node n, void *data, uint8_t *out, int cap);

types.name: cw_state_load_fn
types.decl: typedef void (*cw_state_load_fn)(cw_node n, void *data, const uint8_t *in, int len);

types.name: cw_rollback
types.decl: typedef struct cw_rollback cw_rollback;

types.name: cw_rollback_desc
cw_rollback_stats
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_rollback_stats {
  uint32_t rollbacks;      /* restores */
  uint32_t resim_ticks;    /* ticks re-simulated */
  uint32_t max_depth;      /* deepest rollback, ticks */
  uint32_t stalls;         /* ticks not advanced: prediction window full */
  uint32_t sync_waits;     /* ticks not advanced: time sync */
  uint32_t mispredictions; /* received inputs that differed from the prediction used */
  uint32_t hashes_checked, desyncs;
  int64_t first_desync_tick; /* -1 = none */
  double rollback_ms_total, rollback_ms_max; /* restore + re-simulation wall time */
  double save_ms_total;    /* snapshot wall time */
  uint32_t frames;         /* advance calls */
  uint32_t state_bytes;    /* last snapshot's size */
} cw_rollback_stats;

macros.name: CW_ROLLBACK_MAX_INPUT
macros.doc:
── rollback ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Drives a tree's fixed step from inputs. Each player's input for a tick is
input_size opaque bytes (the game packs buttons and quantized axes). The
local input for tick T + input_delay is sampled at tick T and sent to every
peer (redundantly, unreliable); a remote input not yet received is
predicted as that player's last received one. When a received input
differs from the prediction a past tick used, the tree is restored to the
snapshot before that tick and re-simulated up to now. The local sim never
runs more than max_prediction ticks past the last tick whose inputs are
all known (it stalls instead), and slows down a tick when it is ahead of
the remote by more than one (time sync). Every confirmed state is hashed;
every hash_interval ticks the hash is exchanged and compared (desyncs).

Inside the simulation (node fixed_update), cw_rollback_input(tree, p)
returns player p's input for the tick being simulated: never sample
devices there, and keep every random number on the tree (cw_tree_rng).

headers.summary:
cartwheel noise: coherent random patterns for clouds, terrain, water,
fog density and textures. FastNoiseLite 1.1.1 (MIT, Jordan Peck) wrapped
as cw_noise_*, on the CPU (C) and on the GPU (GLSL and WGSL ports).

  cw_noise n = cw_noise_default();      // OpenSimplex2, frequency 0.01
  n.fractal = CW_NOISE_FRACTAL_FBM;
  n.octaves = 5;
  float h = cw_noise_2d(&n, x, z);       // about -1 .. 1

Patterns (cw_noise_type): OpenSimplex2 (smooth, the general default),
OpenSimplex2S (smoother, a little slower), Cellular (Voronoi cells,
cracks, scales, stones), Perlin, ValueCubic and Value (blocky, cheap).
Fractals stack octaves: FBM (clouds, rolling terrain), Ridged (mountain
ridges, lightning, veins), PingPong (terraces, wood rings). Domain warp
bends the input coordinates by another noise first (swirls, marble,
eroded-looking terrain): cw_noise_warp_2d / _3d.

Determinism. The C code uses only + - * /, integer hashing and float /
int conversions (no libm at all, its square root included: FastNoiseLite
carries its own), so a given cw_noise and input return the same bits on
every host, native and wasm, under the engine's -ffp-contract=off.
Simulation code may use it (terrain heights, spawn maps, buoyancy). The
GPU ports follow the C code line for line; GPUs round differently (fused
multiply-add, division precision), so they agree with the CPU to about
1e-4, not bit for bit: use the CPU result for anything the game state
depends on and the GPU one for pixels.

Costs (one core of the 890M machine, Release): one octave of 2D noise
is 25 ns (Perlin) to 110 ns (OpenSimplex2) a sample, 3D 90 to 160 ns,
cellular 190 ns (2D) and 600 ns (3D); fractals multiply by the octave
count. cw_noise_fill_2d spreads rows over the job pool.

Threading: every function is pure and thread safe.

functions.name: cw_noise_default
functions.doc: FastNoiseLite's defaults (above).

functions.name: cw_noise_2d
functions.signature: float cw_noise_2d(const cw_noise *n, float x, float y)
functions.doc:
One 2D sample, about -1 .. 1 (cellular distances can leave that range; the
texture generator below remaps).

functions.name: cw_noise_3d
functions.signature: float cw_noise_3d(const cw_noise *n, float x, float y, float z)
functions.doc: One 3D sample, about -1 .. 1 (as cw_noise_2d).

functions.name: cw_noise_warp_2d
functions.doc:
Domain warp: move (x, y) by n.warp scaled by n.warp_amp, in place, then
sample another (or the same) cw_noise there. A warp fractal
(WARP_PROGRESSIVE / WARP_INDEPENDENT) runs `octaves` warps. Does nothing
when n.warp is NONE.

functions.name: cw_noise_warp_3d
functions.signature: void cw_noise_warp_3d(const cw_noise *n, float *x, float *y, float *z)
functions.doc: The 3D domain warp: (x, y, z) in place, as cw_noise_warp_2d.

functions.name: cw_noise_fill_2d
functions.signature: void cw_noise_fill_2d(const cw_noise *n, const cw_noise *warp, float *out, int w, int h, float x0, float y0, float step)
functions.doc:
A grid of samples: out[row * w + col] = noise at (x0 + col * step,
y0 + row * step), after warp->warp when warp is non-NULL (a warp of its
own settings, as FastNoiseLite's demo pairs two states). Rows are spread
over the job pool (cw_parallel_for); every value is the same as the
single-sample call, so the result does not depend on the worker count.

functions.name: cw_noise_fill_3d_slice
functions.signature: void cw_noise_fill_3d_slice(const cw_noise *n, const cw_noise *warp, float *out, int w, int h, float x0, float y0, float z, float step)
functions.doc: The 3D form: a slice at depth z (out is w x h), x/y as above.

functions.name: cw_noise_hash
functions.doc: A FNV-1a 64 hash of a grid of samples' bits (for tests and caches).

functions.name: cw_noise_type_name
functions.doc: "opensimplex2", "opensimplex2s", "cellular", "perlin", "value_cubic", "value"

functions.name: cw_noise_type_from_name
functions.doc: -1 when unknown

functions.name: cw_noise_image
functions.signature: bool cw_noise_image(const char *query, uint8_t **rgba, int *w, int *h)
functions.doc:
── generated textures: the gen://noise resource ─────────────────────
cw_res_load("gen://noise?type=perlin&fractal=fbm&octaves=5&size=256",
CW_RES_TEXTURE) makes a texture of noise (cartwheel/resource.h); the path
is its cache key, so the same path loads once and is shared. It is
generated on a worker like an image decode (cw_res_load_async works), is
linear data (not sRGB), RGBA8, repeat-wrapped and mipmapped. Keys (any
order, all optional):

  size=256 | 512x256     texels (1..4096)
  type=opensimplex2      the cw_noise_type name
  seed=1337  freq=0.01   frequency in features per TEXEL (0.01: about 100 texels a feature)
  fractal=none|fbm|ridged|pingpong   octaves=3 lacunarity=2 gain=0.5
  weighted=0 pingpong=2  weighted strength, ping-pong strength
  rotation=none|xy|xz    (with z=)
  cell_dist=euclidean|euclidean_sq|manhattan|hybrid
  cell_return=value|distance|distance2|distance2_add|distance2_sub|distance2_mul|distance2_div
  jitter=1
  warp=none|opensimplex2|opensimplex2_reduced|basic_grid  warp_amp=30 (texels)
  warp_freq=0.005 warp_seed=(seed + 100) warp_fractal=none|progressive|independent warp_octaves=3
  x=0 y=0                offset in texels;  z=   a slice of 3D noise at this depth
  seamless=1             the texture tiles: four shifted copies blended by distance
                         to the edges (the middle loses a little contrast)
  out=gray               r = g = b = the noise, a = 255
      rgba               four layers, seed, seed + 1, seed + 2, seed + 3, one per channel
      normal             a tangent-space normal map of the noise as a height field
                         (strength=2: height units per texel), b up, a = the height
  min=-1 max=1           the noise range mapped to 0 .. 255 (clamped)

Example: clouds "gen://noise?size=512&fractal=fbm&octaves=6&freq=0.004&seamless=1",
water ripples "gen://noise?size=256&type=perlin&fractal=fbm&octaves=4&freq=0.03&out=normal&seamless=1",
stones "gen://noise?type=cellular&cell_return=distance2_sub&freq=0.03".

Generate the same pixels into memory (RGBA8, w x h x 4) without the GPU.
Returns false (logged, naming the key) on a bad query; *w / *h get the
size. The bytes are cw_alloc'd (CW_MEM_RESOURCE): cw_free them.

functions.name: cw_noise_glsl
functions.doc:
── the GPU ports ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Shader source to paste in front of your own (cw_pass_program,
cw_pass_program_wgsl). It defines, in GLSL ES 3.00 and in WGSL:

  float cw_noise2(vec2 p, CwNoise n)       fn cw_noise2(p: vec2f, n: CwNoise) -> f32
  float cw_noise3(vec3 p, CwNoise n)       fn cw_noise3(p: vec3f, n: CwNoise) -> f32
  CwNoise cw_noise_make(int seed, float frequency, int type, int fractal, int octaves)
                                           fn cw_noise_make(...) -> CwNoise
  CwNoise cw_noise_unpack(vec4 a, vec4 b, vec4 c, vec4 d)
                                           fn cw_noise_unpack(...) -> CwNoise

CwNoise is a struct of the cw_noise fields above with enums as int / i32,
in this order: seed, frequency, type (named ntype in WGSL, where type is
reserved), rotation, fractal, octaves, lacunarity, gain,
weighted_strength, ping_pong_strength, cellular_distance,
cellular_return, cellular_jitter. cw_noise_make fills the rest with the
defaults; cw_noise_unpack takes four vec4 uniforms filled from a
cw_noise by cw_noise_gpu_params. Every pattern and fractal of
cw_noise_2d / _3d is there; domain warp is CPU only. Names starting with
cwn_ / CWN_ are the port's own. The tables (gradients, cell offsets) make
each source about 55 KB; a driver compiles it once per program, and
unused functions cost nothing at run time. GPU cost on the 890M: 0.18 ms
a million pixels for one octave of OpenSimplex2, 0.8 ms for five (the
noise guide has the table).

functions.name: cw_noise_wgsl
functions.doc: The WGSL port (as cw_noise_glsl).

functions.name: cw_noise_gpu_params
functions.doc:
n as the 16 floats cw_noise_unpack takes (four vec4: out[0..3], [4..7],
[8..11], [12..15]), the CwNoise fields in order, ints as exact floats,
out[13..15] zero.

types.name: cw_noise_type
cw_noise_rotation
types.doc:
3D only: rotates the lattice so 2D slices (XY or XZ planes) look better.
XZ suits terrain sampled at (x, height, z).
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_NOISE_ROTATION_NONE, CW_NOISE_ROTATION_XY, CW_NOISE_ROTATION_XZ } cw_noise_rotation;

types.name: cw_noise_fractal
cw_noise_cellular_distance
cw_noise_cellular_return
types.doc:
what a cellular sample returns: the nearest cell's random value, the
distance to the nearest point (distance), to the second nearest
(distance2), or a mix of the two (cracks between cells: DISTANCE2_SUB)

types.name: cw_noise_warp
cw_noise
types.doc:
Every setting, FastNoiseLite's, with its default (cw_noise_default). A
plain value: copy it, keep it in a component, hash it.
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_noise {
  int32_t seed;                       /* 1337 */
  float frequency;                    /* 0.01: features per input unit (1 / feature size) */
  cw_noise_type type;                 /* OPENSIMPLEX2 */
  cw_noise_rotation rotation;         /* NONE (3D only) */
  cw_noise_fractal fractal;           /* NONE */
  int32_t octaves;                    /* 3 (fractals) */
  float lacunarity;                   /* 2: frequency multiplier per octave */
  float gain;                         /* 0.5: amplitude multiplier per octave */
  float weighted_strength;            /* 0: 0..1, octaves weighted by the one below (FBM, Ridged) */
  float ping_pong_strength;           /* 2 */
  cw_noise_cellular_distance cellular_distance; /* EUCLIDEAN_SQ */
  cw_noise_cellular_return cellular_return;     /* DISTANCE */
  float cellular_jitter;              /* 1: 0 = a regular grid of points */
  cw_noise_warp warp;                 /* OPENSIMPLEX2: what cw_noise_warp_* use (NONE: no warp) */
  float warp_amp;                     /* 30: warp distance in input units */
} cw_noise;

headers.summary:
Particles and trails: GPU particles in 3D (transform feedback), CPU
particles in 2D (on the render2d batcher), ribbon trails.

── node types (properties: docs/nodes.json, the debug channel's `props`) ──

  GPUParticles3D       (Node3D) `amount` particles simulated on the GPU by
                       transform feedback: per particle position, age,
                       velocity and its spawn cycle, ping-ponged between two
                       buffer pairs every fixed tick. Emission is a pure
                       function of the particle index and sim time (Godot's
                       model): particle i spawns at
                         start + i / amount * lifetime * (1 - explosiveness)
                       and again every `lifetime` seconds while emitting, with
                       its random values hashed from (seed, i, cycle) by an
                       integer hash. No clock is read: the sim advances by the
                       tree's fixed step only, so the same seed and the same
                       number of ticks give the same particles on every host.
    emission           emission_shape POINT / SPHERE / SPHERE_SURFACE / BOX /
                       RING / MESH, emission_extents (box half sizes),
                       emission_radius (+ emission_inner_radius for RING),
                       emission_mesh (a MeshInstance3D node: 4096 points spread
                       over its surface by area, with normals, in that node's
                       space at spawn time), emission_normal_speed (extra speed
                       along the surface normal, SPHERE_SURFACE and MESH)
    motion             direction (local), spread (cone half angle, degrees),
                       speed_min / speed_max, gravity (world), damping,
                       turbulence (strength), turbulence_scale (noise
                       frequency), turbulence_speed (noise scroll): a curl
                       noise field from a 32^3 tiling 3D texture
                       ParticleAttractor3D nodes anywhere in the tree pull
                       (strength > 0) or push every system (up to 8)
    collision          collide_depth: bounce off the scene's depth buffer
                       (screen space: only what the camera sees, surfaces
                       thinner than depth_thickness are solid, normals rebuilt
                       from depth); ParticleCollider3D nodes (PLANE, SPHERE,
                       BOX; up to 8) are analytic; bounce, friction,
                       collision_radius
    look               draw_mode BILLBOARD / STRETCHED (along velocity,
                       stretch x speed) / MESH (mesh_primitive BOX, SPHERE or
                       a mesh_node's mesh, drawn instanced); size, size_random,
                       color (tint), energy (x colour: HDR glow),
                       color_ramp and size_curve (over life, strings below),
                       texture (asset path; default a soft dot), hframes /
                       vframes (flipbook played over life), spin (rad/s,
                       random sign), blend ADD / ALPHA / OPAQUE, soft_distance
                       (fade where particles meet geometry), camera_fade
                       (fade out within this distance of the camera: smoke a
                       chase camera drives into thins instead of filling the
                       screen), sort (ALPHA: back to front with a bitonic
                       sort in fragment passes)
    trails             trail_length (history samples, 0 = off, max 64): each
                       particle draws a camera-facing ribbon through its last
                       positions (one sample per fixed tick, kept in a float
                       texture ring on the GPU), trail_width (tapering to 0)
    lifetime           emitting, amount, lifetime, lifetime_random,
                       explosiveness, one_shot (emits one cycle, then
                       emitting turns off), preprocess (seconds simulated when
                       emission starts), speed_scale, seed, local_coords
                       (particles follow the emitter)
    stats              alive (read-only: particles alive now, computed on the
                       CPU from the same emission function), gpu_stats (read
                       the GPU's own count and position sum back every frame:
                       a stall, for tests), gpu_alive, gpu_sum (read-only)
  ParticleAttractor3D  (Node3D) strength (acceleration at the centre; < 0
                       repels), radius, attenuation (falloff exponent)
  ParticleCollider3D   (Node3D) shape PLANE (the node's XZ plane, normal +Y,
                       extents.xz bounds it; 0 = infinite), SPHERE (radius),
                       BOX (extents = half sizes, particles stay outside)
  GPUParticles2D       (Node2D) the same emission model on the CPU (threaded
                       on the job pool), drawn as sprites through render2d:
                       amount, lifetime, lifetime_random, explosiveness,
                       one_shot, emitting, seed, emission_shape (POINT,
                       CIRCLE, RECT), emission_radius, emission_extents,
                       direction (degrees, 0 = +x), spread, speed_min/max,
                       gravity, damping, size, size_random, color,
                       color_ramp, size_curve, texture, blend (ALPHA, ADD),
                       spin, local_coords, alive (read-only)
  Trail3D              (Node3D) a ribbon that follows the node: the last
                       `length` positions (one per fixed tick) as a camera
                       facing strip of `width`, color_ramp along its length
                       (0 = head), blend

Curves are strings of "t value" stops (t in 0..1, linear between stops):
  size_curve  "0 0.2, 0.15 1, 1 0"
  color_ramp  "0 1 0.8 0.3 0, 0.1 1 0.6 0.2 1, 1 0.4 0.1 0.1 0" (t r g b a)
An empty string is constant 1 (white, full size).

Rendering. Every GPUParticles3D (and Trail3D) of a tree draws in the
pipeline's "particles" EFFECTS pass (order 200): after the opaque scene and
the sky, depth tested against the scene, unlit (the colour is the light:
the scene is HDR, so energy > 1 blooms). The pass reads CW_RES_DEPTH (soft
particles and depth collision sample ctx->depth_tex), so a tree with
particles renders offscreen. The simulation runs in the same pass, one
transform feedback draw per pending fixed tick (no draw happens while the
tree is paused). Costs: one TF draw per system per tick (amount vertices),
one instanced draw per system per frame (plus one for trails); sorting adds
log2(n)(log2(n)+1)/2 full-target passes over a 2^k texel key texture;
gpu_stats adds a scatter, a reduction and a 1-pixel readback (a stall).
On WebGPU (cartwheel/gpu.h) the simulation, the sort and the gpu_stats
reduction are compute passes and the draws read the particle buffers
directly; gpu_alive / gpu_sum arrive asynchronously, never as a stall: a
frame or more after the state they describe (between frames in carts).
Same seed, same alive counts on both backends; position sums agree to
float rounding.
GPU capability: float colour targets (RGBA32F) for sort, trails and
gpu_stats (every host cartwheel supports has them; their absence is logged
and those features are refused, never silently swapped).

GPUParticles2D simulates in fixed_update (CPU, deterministic: cw_rng-free
integer hashes, the deterministic math of cartwheel/math.h) and draws in
the 2D pass as one cw_r2d_sprites batch.

functions.name: cw_particles_restart
functions.doc:
Restart emission of a GPUParticles3D or GPUParticles2D now: every particle
dies and the emission window starts at the current sim time (emitting is
set).

functions.name: cw_particles_alive
functions.doc:
Particles alive now (GPUParticles3D / GPUParticles2D); the same number as
the `alive` property.

functions.name: cw_particles_burst
functions.signature: void cw_particles_burst(cw_node n, t3_vec3 at, t3_vec3 dir)
functions.doc:
A GPUParticles3D with bursts > 0: fire its next burst slot (the oldest
reused) once at world position at, its particles' direction dir (zero:
the system's direction). The slot's amount / bursts particles spawn as a
one-shot of that system would (the same lifetime, explosiveness, shape,
speeds, forces and look), each firing with a new seed. A pool of one-shot
effects becomes one system and one draw, where a system each cost a
simulation pass and a draw whenever any was alive. No-op for another node
or bursts 0. Render only.

functions.name: cw_particles_get_stats
functions.doc: last frame's counts; zeroed when the tree has no particles or t is NULL

functions.name: cw_particle_hash
functions.doc:
The deterministic per-particle hash the GPU uses (a 32-bit integer
finalizer): exposed so tests and tools reproduce emission on the CPU.

types.name: cw_particles_stats
types.doc: Tree totals, for profilers and debug fields.

headers.summary:
cartwheel physics: thin wrappers over Box2D v3 (2D) and Box3D (3D) with
PARALLEL APIs. This header holds what both share; physics2d.h and
physics3d.h hold the per-dimension functions, which mirror each other
name for name (cw_world2d_step / cw_world3d_step, cw_body2d_create /
cw_body3d_create, ...). Including this header includes both.

What the wrapper adds over the raw libraries (and nothing else; every
handle has a *_raw() accessor returning the library id for the rest):
  - worlds stepped on the engine job pool (cartwheel/physics_tasks.h);
  - 32 named collision layers per world, mapped to filter bits;
  - one per-step EVENT LIST (contacts, sensors, hits, joint breaks) in the
    libraries' deterministic order, no allocation per event;
  - queries (ray / shape cast / overlap) filling caller arrays, sorted
    deterministically, plus a batched ray cast on the job pool;
  - character movers (move-and-slide on the libraries' mover APIs);
  - transform sync: bodies bound to a three.c object or a plain transform,
    interpolated between the last two fixed steps at render time;
  - debug draw into a flat line list; stats and a per-step state hash.

Handles: worlds, bodies, shapes and joints are the libraries' own
generational ids packed into 64 bits (b2Store*Id / b3Store*Id), so a
stale handle reads as invalid, never as another object. The null handle
is 0.

Ownership the libraries' user-data slots: cartwheel uses the WORLD's and
the BODY's and the JOINT's user data for its own records. Use
cw_body*_set_user / cw_joint*_set_user instead. Shape user data is yours
(cw_shape*_def.user). Bodies and joints you create through the raw
library API must leave their user data NULL (the wrapper then ignores
them in sync and events, but still hashes their motion).

Determinism: everything that feeds the simulation (movers, queries,
events, the state hash) uses only + - * / sqrt and cartwheel/math.h. The
render-time interpolation is not simulation and may differ in the last
bit between hosts; never feed it back into game state.

Threads: every function here is main-thread only, except that query
functions may run concurrently with each other (never with a step or a
world change). The batched ray cast does exactly that on the job pool.

functions.name: cw_phys_material_default
functions.doc: friction 0.6, the rest 0

functions.name: cw_phys_filter_all
functions.doc: Filter for every non-sensor shape on every layer (same as passing NULL).

functions.name: cw_phys_filter_layers
functions.doc: Filter for the non-sensor shapes on the given layer bits.

functions.name: cw_phys_lines_clear
functions.doc: Empties the list, keeping its capacity.

functions.doc: Number of segments in the list.

functions.name: cw_phys_lines_add

functions.name: cw_phys_lines_free

types.name: cw_phys_material
types.doc:
Surface material. friction 0..1 (mixed sqrt(a*b)), restitution 0..1
(mixed max), rolling_resistance 0..1 (circles/spheres/capsules), tangent
speed for conveyors (2D: along the surface; 3D: tangent_velocity in the
shape's local frame), user_material: your id for sound/particle lookup,
reported in hit events and query hits.

types.name: cw_phys_event_type
types.doc:
── events ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
After each step the world holds one event list, read with
cw_world*_events() and valid until the next step. Order (fixed, and
within each kind the library's own deterministic order):
  contact begin, contact end, hit, sensor enter, sensor exit, joint break.
Contact events need contact_events on BOTH shapes (the default), hit
events need hit_events on one shape and an approach speed above the
world's hit_speed, sensor events need sensor_events on the sensor and on
the visitor (the default). For END/EXIT events the shape may already be
destroyed: then body_a/body_b are null.

types.name: cw_phys_filter
types.doc:
── query filter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
layers: which layers a query hits (CW_PHYS_ALL_LAYERS = all).
sensors: also report sensor shapes. ignore_body: skip this body's shapes
(the caster itself), as a packed body handle (cw_body2d.id / cw_body3d.id).
fn: optional per-shape filter (shape handle id, ctx) -> keep; it runs on
the querying thread (a job-pool thread for batched rays).

types.name: cw_phys_stats
types.doc: ── stats (publish as debug fields: cw_debug_i32("phys.bodies", &s.bodies))

types.name: cw_phys_lines
types.doc:
── debug draw output ────────────────────────────────────────────────
A flat line-segment list (2D lines have z = 0) that any renderer can draw
as GL_LINES: pos holds 6 floats per segment (x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1), color one
0xRRGGBB per segment. cw_world*_debug_draw APPENDS; clear between frames
with cw_phys_lines_clear (keeps capacity: no allocation once warm).

types.name: cw_joint_type
types.doc:
── joints: one type enum for both dimensions ────────────────────────
Which exist where (the libraries' own set):
  both: DISTANCE, FILTER (no collision between two bodies), MOTOR,
        PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE, WELD, WHEEL, MOUSE (a motor joint from an
        internal kinematic body named "cw_mouse", moved to the target
        each step: drag with a pointer)
  3D only: SPHERICAL (ball and socket, cone + twist limits), PARALLEL
        (keeps z axes aligned: keep a body upright)
  2D only: MOVER (Box2D v3.2's dynamic character mover: a velocity command on a dynamic body, x and y
        separately, limited by a force; no rotation), POGO (a spring along a normal that holds a dynamic
        character off the ground, with a tension and a compression limit)

macros.name: CW_PHYS_LAYERS
macros.doc:
── collision layers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
A shape sits on ONE layer (0..31, category bit 1<<layer) and collides
with the layers in its mask (bit i = layer i). Two shapes collide when
each one's mask holds the other's layer, unless both share a nonzero
group: negative = never collide, positive = always.

Bits above 31 are reserved for queries: every non-sensor shape accepts
queries, sensors only when a query asks for them (cw_phys_filter.sensors).
Do not set shape filters through the raw library APIs.

headers.summary:
cartwheel 2D physics: Box2D v3 (deps/box2d), mirrored name for name by
physics3d.h. Read physics.h first: layers, events, filters, stats, debug
lines and the handle/ownership rules are shared and documented there.

Typical frame:
  init:          w = cw_world2d_create(&def); bodies, shapes, joints
  fixed_update:  movers / forces / kinematic targets, cw_world2d_step(w, dt),
                 then read cw_world2d_events(w, &n)
  render:        cw_world2d_sync(w, alpha) writes bound objects

Vectors are cw_vec2 (same layout as b2Vec2). Rotations are a unit
(cos, sin) pair, Box2D's b2Rot: no trig in the simulation path; use
cw_rot2_angle / cw_rot2_from_angle (cartwheel/math.h, deterministic) to
convert. Units: meters, kilograms, seconds, radians. y is up.

headers.summary:
cartwheel 3D physics: Box3D (deps/box3d), mirrored name for name by
physics2d.h. Read physics.h first: layers, events, filters, stats, debug
lines and the handle/ownership rules are shared and documented there.

Typical frame:
  init:          w = cw_world3d_create(&def); bodies, shapes, joints
  fixed_update:  movers / forces / kinematic targets, cw_world3d_step(w, dt),
                 then read cw_world3d_events(w, &n)
  render:        cw_world3d_sync(w, alpha) writes bound three.c objects

Vectors and rotations are three.c's t3_vec3 / t3_quat (same layout as
Box3D's b3Vec3 / b3Quat). Units: meters, kilograms, seconds, radians.

functions.name: cw_world3d_default_def
functions.doc: The defaults noted in cw_world3d_def above.

functions.name: cw_world3d_create
functions.doc: Creates a Box3D world stepped on the job pool. Up to 128 worlds.

functions.name: cw_world3d_destroy
functions.doc: Destroys every body, shape, joint and record of the world.

functions.name: cw_world3d_valid
functions.doc: False for null, destroyed or stale handles.

functions.name: cw_world3d_step
functions.doc:
One fixed step of dt seconds: drives mouse joints, steps Box3D, then
builds the event list, breaks overloaded joints, updates the
interpolation pairs of moved bodies and folds the step into the state
hash. Cost: the library step plus O(moved bodies + events).

functions.name: cw_world3d_tick_begin
functions.doc:
For a world stepped more than once a fixed tick (shorter steps for fast
bodies): call it at the start of every tick, before the tick's first step.
Interpolation (cw_world3d_sync, cw_body3d_interpolated) then runs from each
body's pose at the start of the tick to its pose after the tick's last
step, the span the render callback's alpha measures. Without it the pair is
the last step's alone: alpha would move a body over a fraction of the
tick while everything interpolated per tick (a camera) moves over all of
it, and the body would shift against them as alpha changes.

functions.name: cw_world3d_events
functions.doc: Sets *count; NULL (count 0) for an invalid world. The array belongs to the world.

functions.name: cw_world3d_sync
functions.doc:
Writes every bound body's transform, interpolated between the last two
steps (the last tick's start and end with cw_world3d_tick_begin) by alpha
(the render callback's), into its three.c object or plain transform.
Bodies that did not move in the last step (tick) are written once and then
skipped.

functions.name: cw_world3d_stats
functions.doc: Counters, step count and state hash; all zero for an invalid world. Cheap.

functions.name: cw_world3d_shift_origin
functions.doc:
Floating origin (cartwheel/stream.h): move every body by -shift, in
creation order, keeping velocities, sleep states and the interpolation
(synced objects do not jump). Box3D has no origin shift of its own, so
this sets each body's transform: O(bodies), for a rare event. Joint
anchors on the world itself (cw_joint3d to no body, mouse targets) do not
move: move them yourself. Deterministic: called on a tick the simulation
picks, every host shifts the same bodies by the same amount.

functions.name: cw_heightfield3d_create
functions.signature: cw_heightfield3d cw_heightfield3d_create(const uint16_t *q, int nx, int nz, t3_vec3 scale, const uint8_t *materials)
functions.doc:
Height fields (resources, like collision meshes): Box3D's grid of nx x nz
samples (x along columns, z along rows; sample (i, j) at local
(i * scale.x, q[j * nx + i] * scale.y, j * scale.z)), stored as the uint16
steps given, exactly. Each quad splits along the diagonal from its
(i, j + 1) corner to its (i + 1, j) corner. materials: (nx - 1) x (nz - 1)
cell bytes (0xFF = a hole, no collision), NULL = all 0. Fields that share
a scale.y line up exactly along shared edges (cartwheel/terrain.h tiles
them). Null (logged) for fewer than 2 x 2 samples.

types.doc:
── character mover ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
A kinematic capsule outside the simulation (Box3D's mover API, which is
EXPERIMENTAL upstream: deps/box3d/docs/character.md), moved with
move-and-slide: you set velocity (input + gravity), cw_mover3d_move
moves as far as the world allows, slides along surfaces, walks up slopes
up to max_floor_angle, steps up ledges up to step_height, snaps down to
the floor within snap_length, rides moving platforms and clips the
velocity against what it hit. Sensors never block it.

Plain struct, owned by the caller; fields below the def are outputs.
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_mover3d_def {
  float radius, height;        /* capsule, feet to top: 0.3, 1.8 */
  t3_vec3 up;                  /* (0, 1, 0) */
  float max_floor_angle;       /* radians: 45 degrees */
  float step_height;           /* 0.3; 0 = no stepping */
  float snap_length;           /* 0.25; 0 = no snapping */
  float skin;                  /* contact detection distance: 0.02 (<= 0 becomes 0.02) */
  int max_iterations;          /* slide iterations per move: 5 */
  uint32_t mask;               /* layers it collides with (queries never see sensors): all */
  float push_mass;             /* >0: pushes dynamic bodies as this mass */
  bool ride_platforms;         /* inherit the floor body's velocity: true */
} cw_mover3d_def;

headers.summary:
Physics nodes: the scene tree's layer over the Box2D / Box3D wrappers
(physics.h). The 2D and 3D sets mirror each other name for name.

── node types ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  CollisionObject2D/3D  (abstract) collision_layer is an INDEX 0..31 (a
                        body's shapes sit on ONE layer, physics.h) while
                        collision_mask is a BIT SET: layer = 1, mask = 5
                        means "on layer 1, collides with layers 0 and 2"
                        (Godot uses bits for both). Prefer the name forms
                        collision_layer_name / collision_mask_names
                        ("world|enemy"), resolved against the project's
                        layer names (below). An unknown name is logged as
                        an error (cw_error): the layer stays as it was, a
                        mask leaves that name out.
  PhysicsBody2D/3D      (abstract) friction, bounce, rolling_resistance,
                        tangent_speed (2D conveyor, px/s) / tangent_velocity
                        (3D, m/s, shape-local), user_material,
                        contact_monitor (emit body_entered/body_exited on
                        contact begin/end), hit_events (emit body_hit(other,
                        speed) above the world's hit speed).
  StaticBody2D/3D       never moves by itself; moving the node teleports it.
  KinematicBody2D/3D    follows the node's global transform: every tick
                        the body is given the velocity that reaches it
                        (pushes rigid bodies, carries characters).
  RigidBody2D/3D        density, mass (0 = from density), gravity_scale,
                        linear_damp, angular_damp, lock_rotation, bullet,
                        can_sleep, freeze + freeze_mode (STATIC|KINEMATIC:
                        the runtime body-type switch), linear_velocity,
                        angular_velocity (live), sleeping (read-only).
                        Its transform is written into the node after every
                        step; setting position/rotation teleports it.
  CharacterBody2D/3D    velocity, floor_max_angle, floor_snap_length,
                        step_height, max_slides, push_mass, ride_platforms;
                        read-only on_floor, on_wall, on_ceiling,
                        floor_normal, wall_normal, platform_velocity.
                        Moves only through cw_character*_move_and_slide
                        (call it from fixed_update). Its shape (the first
                        CollisionShape child: capsule, circle/sphere or
                        rect/box) sizes the mover; a kinematic proxy body
                        with the same shapes sits at the mover each step so
                        areas, rays and other characters see it.
  Area2D/3D             monitoring, monitorable; sensor shapes. Signals
                        body_entered(node), body_exited(node),
                        area_entered(node), area_exited(node); read-only
                        overlap_count. Areas move with their node.
                        DETECTION IS TWO-SIDED: an area sees a body only
                        when the area's mask has the body's layer AND the
                        body's mask has the area's layer (Box2D/Box3D
                        filter both ways; Godot checks one side). Give a
                        player a mask such as "world|pickups|hazards".
                        A shape's `disabled` (and any shape property) may
                        change at run time: the body is rebuilt before the
                        next step and overlaps begin / end then.
  CollisionShape2D      shape (RECT|CIRCLE|CAPSULE|POLYGON|SEGMENT|CHAIN),
                        size, radius, height, points ("x y, x y, ..." local
                        pixels; POLYGON may be concave: it is triangulated),
                        loop (CHAIN), disabled. Direct child of a body or
                        area; its own position/rotation/scale place it.
                        CHAIN: one-sided segments. Open: walking the points
                        on screen the solid side is on your LEFT (a ground
                        line is listed right to left), and every authored
                        segment collides (Box2D's ghost end vertices are
                        added past the ends). loop: solid inside whatever
                        the winding.
  CollisionShape3D      shape (BOX|SPHERE|CAPSULE|CONVEX|TRIMESH), size,
                        radius, height, points ("x y z, ..."), mesh (path
                        to a MeshInstance3D or a baked CSG root, whose
                        geometry CONVEX/TRIMESH use when points is
                        empty), disabled. TRIMESH: static bodies only.
  Joint2D/3D            joint_type (2D: PIN HINGE SLIDER DISTANCE SPRING
                        WELD WHEEL MOTOR; 3D adds CONE (ball and socket
                        with a cone limit)), node_a, node_b (paths relative
                        to the joint; empty node_a = the world), anchor =
                        the joint's global position, axis = its local x
                        (2D) / z (3D: hinge axis) / x (3D slider);
                        collide_connected, break_force, break_torque,
                        limit_enabled, lower, upper, motor_enabled,
                        motor_speed, max_motor, stiffness (Hz), damping,
                        length (0 = current), cone_angle. Signal broken.
                        Motor/limit/spring changes apply in place; other
                        changes rebuild the joint.
  RayCast2D/3D          enabled, target_position (local), collision_mask,
                        collide_with_bodies, collide_with_areas,
                        exclude_parent; read-only colliding, collider,
                        collision_point, collision_normal, collision_fraction.
  ShapeCast2D/3D        shape (2D: CIRCLE RECT CAPSULE; 3D: SPHERE BOX
                        CAPSULE), radius, size, height, target_position
                        (zero = overlap test), max_results, the ray's
                        filters; read-only colliding, collision_count and
                        the closest hit's collider/point/normal/fraction.

Units: 2D nodes are canvas pixels with y DOWN; the Box2D world runs in
meters with y up (pixels_per_meter, default 32). 3D nodes are meters.

── worlds and the frame order ───────────────────────────────────────────
One 2D and one 3D world per tree (tree slots "physics2d" / "physics3d"),
created when the first physics node enters. Each fixed tick:
  1. hook (order -100): bodies' nodes snapshot their transform (render
     interpolation start)
  2. nodes' fixed_update in tree order: scripts read last step's results,
     set velocities, call move_and_slide (characters move NOW against the
     current world), move kinematic nodes
  3. deferred structural changes and signals of phase 2 are applied
  4. hook (order 100): node -> body (new/changed shapes, teleports,
     kinematic targets, joints), step 2D then 3D, body -> node for rigid
     bodies, ray/shape casts refresh, then contact / sensor / hit / break
     events become signals, delivered in the library's event order; node
     frees and adds from those handlers are deferred until all are sent
  5. hook (order 200): Camera2D smoothing
This is Godot's order (physics_process, then the physics step), so a
script sees signals from the step that followed its last fixed_update.
Consequence: a character riding a KinematicBody platform follows it with
one tick of lag (it moved in step 2, the platform moves in step 4); it is
consistent and deterministic. Snap length + step height also carry a
running character across small gaps (about 1 m at default settings):
level designers should make gaps wider or lower snap/step on the body.
The world does not step while the tree is paused.

Project layer names / settings: an optional asset `project.cwproj` with
lines `layer_names_2d = "world, player, coins"`, `layer_names_3d = ...`,
`gravity_2d = vec2(0, 980)` (px/s^2, y down), `gravity_3d = vec3(0, -9.8,
0)`, `pixels_per_meter = 32`, `substeps = 4`; or cw_physics_nodes_config
before the first physics node enters a tree.

headers.summary:
Box2D / Box3D on the engine job pool.

cw_box2d_tasks / cw_box3d_tasks fill a world def's task callbacks so the
physics step runs on cartwheel's one thread pool (cartwheel/jobs.h). Pass
workers = 0 for every pool thread, or a smaller count to cap it (the
library splits its work by this count; results do not depend on it:
Box2D v3 and Box3D are deterministic across worker counts).

functions.name: cw_box2d_tasks
functions.doc:
Sets def->workerCount and the task callbacks (one pool job per Box2D task); allocates a small per-world context in
def->userTaskContext (free it with cw_box2d_tasks_release, after b2DestroyWorld). Workers capped at B2_MAX_WORKERS
(32).

functions.doc: Free what cw_box2d_tasks allocated (def.userTaskContext), after b2DestroyWorld.

functions.name: cw_box3d_tasks
functions.doc:
Sets def->workerCount and the task callbacks (one pool job per Box3D task); allocates a small per-world context in
def->userTaskContext (free it with cw_box3d_tasks_release, after b3DestroyWorld).

functions.name: cw_box3d_tasks_release
functions.doc: Free what cw_box3d_tasks allocated (def.userTaskContext), after b3DestroyWorld.

functions.doc:
Call before each b2World_Step / b3World_Step: decides, from the world's awake bodies, whether this step's tasks run
on the pool or on the calling thread.

functions.name: cw_box3d_tasks_step

macros.name: CW_PHYSICS_POOL_MIN_AWAKE
macros.doc:
Fewer awake bodies than this and a step runs every task on the calling thread: a small world's step is a fraction
of a millisecond, and fanning it out to the pool (Box3D's per-stage tasks, the solver's spin-synced workers) costs
many times the work. The world keeps its workerCount, so the result is the same either way.

headers.summary:
The render pipeline: a small per-tree frame graph of passes.

Every tree that draws 3D owns one pipeline (created on first use). The
scene runner (cw_scene_app) renders through it every frame, so scene apps
get it without doing anything; other apps call cw_pipeline_render. A frame
runs the active passes phase by phase, and inside a phase by `order`
(ascending; ties in registration order):

  CW_PHASE_SHADOW    targets of the pass's own: nothing is bound for it.
                     (three.c still renders its own light shadows inside
                     the scene pass.) Module
                     pass: "visibility" (2000, visibility.h: culling, LOD,
                     impostor bakes; it hides culled meshes for the frame).
  CW_PHASE_PREPASS   depth-only draws into the scene FBO. The built-in
                     "depth_prepass" (settings.depth_prepass) is one. When
                     any prepass ran, the scene pass keeps that depth and
                     clears colour only.
  CW_PHASE_OPAQUE    the scene: the built-in "scene" pass (order 0) renders
                     the tree's three.c scene (opaque, background,
                     transparent, as three.c orders them) into the scene
                     FBO (HDR colour + depth texture, or the MSAA
                     renderbuffers). Passes after it here draw more
                     geometry with the same depth. Module passes:
                     "impostors" (100) and "occlusion_queries" (900:
                     bounding boxes against the finished depth),
                     visibility.h.
  CW_PHASE_SKY       background / atmosphere after the opaque scene, into
                     the scene FBO, depth-tested against the scene.
  CW_PHASE_EFFECTS   particles, decals, fog volumes: the scene FBO with its
                     depth attached for testing; ctx->depth_tex is a copy
                     to SAMPLE. (With MSAA the scene is resolved before
                     SKY, so these phases draw single-sampled.) Module
                     passes: "decals" (100, decals.h), "particles" (200,
                     particles.h: GPU particle simulation and drawing,
                     trails).
  CW_PHASE_POST      the full-screen chain. A pass that WRITES CW_RES_COLOR
                     reads ctx->src and writes ctx->dst; the pipeline
                     ping-pongs pooled targets and hands the last writer
                     the output as dst. A pass that only reads sees the
                     current image as src (after the last writer that is
                     the output: tex 0 when it is the screen). Built-ins:
                     "velocity" (0, when something reads CW_RES_VELOCITY),
                     "ssao" (100), "taa" (200), "dof" (250), "bloom" (300), "tonemap"
                     (500, HDR to display), "grade" (550, 3D LUT), "aa"
                     (600, FXAA or SMAA), "lens" (700: chromatic
                     aberration, vignette, film grain), "debug_view"
                     (10000).
  CW_PHASE_OVERLAY   2D, UI and debug draw into the output (display
                     values, no depth). Built-ins: "canvas" (-100: the
                     tree's 2D pass and its cw_canvas_add_pass UI overlays,
                     cartwheel/scene2d.h; it clears first when no 3D was
                     drawn) and "app" (0: the app's render callback, so a
                     HUD lands on top). Debug draw at 1000 is the
                     convention. render2d draws to the window: with a
                     custom output (cw_pipeline_set_output) an overlay pass
                     targets ctx->output itself.
  CW_PHASE_PRESENT   last: readbacks, captures, a final scale when the
                     output is not the screen. Module pass:
                     "visibility_restore" (1000) shows what "visibility"
                     hid.

The scene is always linear HDR: three.c (three.js r187's generated
programs, physical light units, colour management) renders it into the
RGBA16F scene target, and the "tonemap" POST pass applies exposure, the
tone curve and the sRGB transfer function.

── adding a pass (what another module does) ─────────────────────────

  static void fog_exec(cw_pass_ctx *ctx, void *user) {
    // EFFECTS: the scene FBO is bound (colour + depth for testing)
    glUseProgram(fog_prog);
    cw_pass_bind_texture(0, ctx->depth_tex); // the copy: safe to sample
    glEnable(GL_BLEND);
    glBlendFunc(GL_ONE, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
    cw_pass_fullscreen();                    // one triangle, no buffers
  }
  if (!cw_pipeline_has_pass(cw_pipeline_of(tree), "height_fog"))
    cw_pipeline_add_pass(cw_pipeline_of(tree), &(cw_pass_desc){
        .name = "height_fog", .phase = CW_PHASE_EFFECTS, .order = 300,
        .reads = CW_RES_DEPTH, .writes = CW_RES_COLOR,
        .active = fog_active, .execute = fog_exec, .user = my_state });

A module registers its passes once per tree: from a node type's
enter_tree (a HeightFog node), from cw_tree_add_hook, or from app init.
Rules a pass follows:
  - Raw GL is fine. The pipeline forgets three.c's cached GL state
    (t3_renderer_reset_bindings) before every three.c render it makes. A
    pass that calls t3_renderer_render itself (shadow casters, probes)
    calls t3_renderer_reset_bindings(ctx->renderer) first and puts the
    renderer's framebuffer, render target and size back afterwards.
  - Before execute the pipeline binds the phase's target and viewport (see
    above), and leaves depth test, blending, culling and scissor OFF and
    the colour mask on; a pass enables what it uses. A pass may bind other
    targets (cw_pass_bind_target); POST writers must leave their result in
    ctx->dst, or in a target of their own named by ctx->result.
  - Declare what you read and write (CW_RES_*). The graph uses it: reading
    DEPTH or VELOCITY moves the scene offscreen, VELOCITY schedules the
    velocity pass, DEPTH in SKY / EFFECTS makes the depth copy, COLOR
    writes in POST join the ping-pong chain.
  - active() switches a pass per frame from settings (cheap, no GL); the
    user switch is cw_pipeline_set_pass_enabled.
  - Scratch targets come from the pool: cw_pass_rt(ctx, w, h, format) is
    yours until the frame ends (or cw_pass_rt_release). Targets that
    outlive a frame (history) are cw_pipeline_rt_persistent.
  - Every pass is timed on the GPU (GL_TIME_ELAPSED where the host has
    EXT_disjoint_timer_query; natively on WebGPU through timestamp
    queries, never in a cart) and on the CPU (its execute):
    cw_pipeline_pass_stats, the debug channel's "pipeline" command.
  - WebGPU (cartwheel/gpu.h): a pass runs there only with webgpu = true in
    its desc. It draws through the same helpers with a WGSL program
    (cw_pass_program_wgsl, cw_pass_use, cw_pass_set_blend / _depth,
    cw_pass_clear, cw_pass_fullscreen / cw_pass_draw); every pass records
    into one command encoder per pipeline frame. Offscreen targets keep
    GL's row order and depth is GL's [0, 1] window depth, so GLSL ports
    line for line. ctx->depth_tex is an R32F LINEAR depth there (view-space
    distance, 3e38 where nothing was drawn; read it with textureLoad /
    cw_load). MSAA (4x, WebGPU's only count) serves any scene on a core
    WebGPU device (the multisampled depth's sample 0 is resolved into the
    scene depth when the opaque phase ends, as GL's blit does); in
    compatibility mode only RGBA8 scenes without depth readers. three.c has no WebGPU backend yet: the "scene"
    pass is skipped, and an OPAQUE pass of the app's (webgpu = true) can
    draw the scene (samples/post_synth).
  - Under TAA the camera's projection_matrix carries this frame's jitter
    while the passes run (it is restored after); ctx->proj / view_proj are
    the unjittered ones.
  - Fragment shaders get highp samplers from cw_pass_program; GLSL ES
    defaults sampler2D to lowp in fragment shaders, which quantizes depth
    and HDR on some GPUs.

The workflow is three.js r187's: material and environment colours are
linear, lights are physical units (see "Light units" below), and the post
chain works on scene-linear HDR until the tonemap pass.

The program states the tree's last frame needed and none of the app's
program tables has, one per line ("" when none). A cart skips those draws;
a native build with CW_THREE_BUILDER builds them at run time. Either way
each line belongs in the app's table (cmake/programs.cmake: run
tools/programs.mjs). Also the debug fields "cw.three.missing" (the count)
and "cw.three.missing_states" (the lines; the gates fail on them), and the
"pipeline" command.

Render one frame of the tree into the output (the bound default
framebuffer unless cw_pipeline_set_output), w x h pixels. The scene runner
calls this; apps without the runner call it from their render callback.

functions.doc:
Render into this target instead of the screen (NULL = the screen). The
target is not owned.

Set the views (n <= 1: the tree's current camera fills the output, as
without views). Copied.

functions.name: cw_pipeline_views
functions.doc: The views in use (0 when a single camera fills the output).

functions.name: cw_pipeline_split
functions.signature: int cw_pipeline_split(cw_pipeline *p, const cw_node *cameras, int n)
functions.doc:
A split of the output for n players: 2 side by side (top / bottom when
the output is taller than wide), 3 and 4 as quadrants (3 leaves the last
quadrant to the HUD), cameras taken in order. Returns the count set.

functions.name: cw_pipeline_set_view_hook
functions.signature: void cw_pipeline_set_view_hook(cw_pipeline *p, void (*hook)(int view, void *user), void *user)
functions.doc:
Called before each view's 3D picture is drawn, with the view's index:
something can be posed one way in one player's view and another way in
the rest (a player's own replay, say). NULL: none. Shared work is done
with the first view, as the hook left it: the shadow maps, and the
scene's world matrices (what a hook moves for a later view, it updates
itself, t3_object_update_world_matrix).

functions.name: cw_pipeline_set_views_shared_post
functions.doc:
Splitscreen's post chain, shared: each view runs only the post passes that
read its depth or motion (SSAO, say) and keeps its picture in HDR; the
views are laid out first and the rest of the chain (bloom, tone mapping,
the grade, anti-aliasing, lens effects) runs once over the whole output.
A view then costs its 3D and those passes, not a whole chain (the CPU
records each pass once a frame instead of once a view). The vignette and
the bloom are the screen's then, not each view's: a glow can cross a seam.
Off by default.

format targets are reused across frames, so this costs no allocation in a
steady state. with_depth adds a DEPTH_COMPONENT24 texture.

after the version line (precision highp is prepended; `in vec2 v_uv` is
provided). Returns 0 and logs the compiler output on failure. GL only (a
WebGPU run logs an error and returns 0: use cw_pass_program_wgsl).

Depth of the following draws on a target with depth: test (LESS) and
write (reset to off before every pass). write without test always writes
(a full-screen pass that outputs depth).

functions.doc:
Procedural geometry without buffers: `vertices` vertices as a triangle
list, positioned by the program's own vertex stage from the vertex index
(gl_VertexID / @builtin(vertex_index)): a GLSL program from
cw_pass_program_vs, or a WGSL module that defines `@vertex fn vs`. On
WebGPU that vertex stage writes clip z as (z + w) / 2 for GL's depth range
and multiplies clip y by cw_target.flip (offscreen targets keep GL's row
order).

functions.signature: unsigned cw_pass_program_vs(const char *name, const char *vs, const char *fs)
functions.doc:
cw_pass_program with a vertex stage of its own (GLSL ES 3.00 after the
version line) for cw_pass_draw.

functions.name: cw_pass_bind_texture
functions.doc:
Bind tex to texture unit `unit` (GL_TEXTURE_2D). On WebGPU tex is the
registry id a cw_rt carries (rt->tex), ctx->depth_tex, or a LUT's.

functions.name: cw_pass_bind_texture_3d

functions.name: cw_pass_texture_new
functions.signature: unsigned cw_pass_texture_new(int w, int h, cw_rt_format f, const void *texels)
functions.doc:
A texture of your own for pass programs (a lookup table, a noise image, a
CPU-made mask): w x h texels of format f, uploaded once. RGBA8 and R8 take
bytes, RGBA16F / RG16F / R16F take IEEE halves, packed rows (no padding),
row 0 first as glTexImage2D takes it (row 0 is v = 0, the bottom, in
GLSL's texture() and in WGSL through the offscreen row order). Linear
filtered, clamped to the edge, no mips. Returns an id for
cw_pass_bind_texture on GL and WebGPU alike, 0 (logged) on bad arguments.
Needs the GPU (init or later). Free it with cw_pass_texture_free.

functions.doc:
Probed on first use (needs the GL context: call from init or later).
Measured on Linux with Mesa (2026-10): RGBA16F renders and timer

romdev's wasmcart host and in Chromium (wasmcart's web host enables

A render target: an FBO with one colour texture (linear filtered, clamped)
and optionally a depth texture. Read-only to users. fbo 0 with tex 0 is the
output when it is the screen (never sample it).

types.doc:
Tone curves, three.js r187's (ToneMappingFunctions): NONE clamps; AGX
(Blender's AgX, three.js's minimal fit) is the default; NEUTRAL is Khronos
PBR Neutral. The sRGB transfer follows every curve, as in r187.

types.doc:
Post antialiasing on display values. FXAA: 3.11, quality preset 12. SMAA:
1x with orthogonal pattern search (16 steps) and corner rounding; its
diagonal pattern search is not built yet. TAA is a separate switch.
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_AA_NONE, CW_AA_FXAA, CW_AA_SMAA } cw_aa_mode;

types.doc:
Show an intermediate buffer instead of the image (the "debug_view" POST
pass, last in the chain): linear depth (1 / (1 + z / 4)), view-space
normals rebuilt from depth, the GTAO visibility (needs ssao), the velocity
(x 20, 0.5 = still), or the bloom chain's result (needs bloom).

types.doc:
Every post setting, with its default. The PostProcess node (docs/nodes.json)
mirrors these as properties for scene files; code can write
cw_pipeline_settings(p) directly. Changing a field takes effect on the next
frame; nothing is ever lowered automatically (quality is the developer's).

  int ssao_slices;          /* 2 directions per pixel (x2 sides) */
  int ssao_steps;           /* 6 horizon steps per side */

cw_pass_desc
cw_view

macros.name: CW_MAX_VIEWS
macros.doc:
A view: a Camera3D drawn into a rectangle of the output (fractions of
it, x / y from the top left). With two or more views the pipeline renders
the 3D scene once per view (each through its own camera, at its own size,
with the post chain minus TAA, whose history one camera owns; the shadow
maps are drawn once, for the first view, and the others reuse them), lays the
pictures into their rectangles, then runs the overlays (the app's HUD,
debug draw) once over the whole output: a HUD reads the rectangles back
with cw_pipeline_views.

headers.summary:
cartwheel platform layer: the app loop, window + GL context, raw input,
time, audio output, assets.

One SDL2 code path serves both builds: native links real SDL2, carts link
wasmcart-sdl2 (SDL2 on the wasmcart ABI). The only differences live in
src/platform/native.c and src/platform/cart.c: who owns the loop, where time
comes from, how audio reaches the device and how assets are read.

The engine owns the frame. A game never writes a main loop: it returns a
cw_app_desc from cw_main() and is called back. Natively cw_main runs from
main(); in a cart from wc_init(), and each wc_render() is one frame.

functions.doc: Provided by the game (or by the engine's scene runner).

functions.name: cw_platform_touch_primary
functions.doc:
True when the device is touch-first and no gamepad has been used: start in
touch mode (draw touch prompts / controls from the first frame). Android
and iOS builds say yes; a desktop says no unless CW_TOUCH_PRIMARY=1. A
cart learns it from its host through the debug channel request
`touch_primary 1` (sent before the first frame: the web export's player
does so for a coarse-pointer browser, run-cart --touch-primary for tests);
other hosts leave it false. Any pad button or stick turns it false for the
rest of the run.

functions.name: cw_platform_vibrate
functions.doc:
A short buzz on a phone (feedback for a touch control's press), ms long.
Presentation only. A cart publishes it as the debug field `cw.vibrate`
(a request count, then ms) and the web export's player calls
navigator.vibrate where the browser has it; other hosts ignore it.

Pixels of what is being drawn right now: the window's, or with

functions.name: cw_asset_size
functions.doc:
── assets (read-only, shipped with the game) ────────────────────────
Paths are relative to the asset root ("fonts/a.ttf", never "assets/..."),
'/'-separated, never containing "..".
Native: the .cwpak named by CW_PAK, else <executable>.cwpak when it exists
(cwpack writes it), then loose files for paths the pack does not hold: the
root is CW_ASSETS if set, else <exe>.assets beside the executable
(cw_add_app's ASSETS dir is linked there), else ./assets.
Cart: the cart's own bundle (the same ASSETS dir or PACK output, packed).
Safe from any thread natively; in a cart call them from the main thread (a
lazily loaded web cart suspends there while the bytes arrive). Most code
loads through cartwheel/resource.h instead. cw_asset_size returns -1 when
the asset does not exist; cw_asset_read returns the bytes copied (at most
cap), -1 when missing.

startup): an editor opening a project directory makes the project's

Caches keyed by path (fonts, textures, scenes) keep what they loaded.
Cart: no-op, returns false (a cart's assets are its bundle).

headers.summary:
cartwheel platformer controller: the feel of a side-view platformer on top of cw_mover2d.

What it adds to the mover: acceleration and braking on the ground and in the air, gravity that is heavier when
falling and when a jump is let go early (variable jump height), corner correction (a head that clips a ceiling corner is carried round it), coyote time (a jump still works for a moment
after walking off a ledge), jump buffering (a press just before landing jumps on landing), air jumps, wall
slide and wall jump (with a grace window after leaving the wall), a dash, dropping through one-way platforms
(down + jump) and swimming (the game says how deep the character is and which way a current pushes).

  cw_platformer2d p;
  cw_platformer2d_init(&p, world, NULL, feet);
  fixed_update:  cw_platformer2d_step(&p, &(cw_platformer2d_input){ .move_x = ax, .jump_held = held,
                                      .jump_pressed = pressed }, dt);
  then read p.events (CW_PF_*) for sounds and particles, p.body.position for the feet.

The step is simulation code: + - * / and sqrt only, the same bits on every host.

headers.summary:
cartwheel plugins: runtime modules a PROJECT adds to the engine
without editing the cartwheel tree.

── What a plugin is ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
A directory <project>/plugins/<name>/ holding plugin.cwplugin (the
manifest, `key = value` lines like project.cwproj) and C sources:

  name = spinner                  C identifier, the same as the directory
  version = 1.2.0                 the plugin's own version (free text)
  engine_api = 1.0                the engine API it was written for
  kind = both                     runtime | editor | both
  runtime_sources = runtime       files/directories (.c, recursive), plugin-relative
  editor_sources = editor         (defaults: runtime/ and editor/)
  provides = Spinner, SpinnerFX   node types it registers (named in errors
                                  when a scene uses them and it is off)
  depends = other_plugin          plugins it needs (loaded first)
  enabled = true
  title = Spinner                 optional, for the editor's Plugins panel
  description = ...

RUNTIME plugins are compiled into the game by the project build (natively
and as a cart): cw_add_app finds <its source dir>/plugins/ (or PLUGINS
<dir>), compiles each enabled runtime plugin and generates the app's
plugin table. The engine registers them at startup, before the app's
init (cw_plugins_init), so scenes loading in init see their node types.
EDITOR plugins are editor modules (cwed/editor.h, CWED_PLUGIN): the native
editor builds and loads them as shared libraries from the project; a cart
editor gets them compiled in by the project build.

── The runtime side of a plugin ───────────────────────────────────────

    #include "cartwheel/plugin.h"
    static void reg(void) { cw_node_type_register(&spinner_type); ... }
    CW_PLUGIN(spinner, .version = "1.2.0", .register_fn = reg);

register_fn runs once at startup (and again after a hot reload of a
native plugin library: re-registering a node type with the same layout
swaps its code, cartwheel/scene.h). It registers through the engine's
ordinary registries; nothing is plugin-specific:

  node types + methods        cartwheel/scene.h  cw_node_type_register, cw_node_type_add_method
  scene file sections         cartwheel/scene_file.h  cw_scene_register_section
  resource types / importers  cartwheel/resource.h  cw_res_register_type
  debug-channel commands      cartwheel/debug.h  cw_debug_command
  render pipeline passes      cartwheel/pipeline.h  (from a node type's enter_tree, per tree)

── The plugin contract (API version) ──────────────────────────────────
The headers a plugin may include are the engine's public headers
(include/cartwheel/, every .h) and, for editor plugins, cwed/editor.h. Their
declarations are the plugin API, versioned as CW_ENGINE_API_MAJOR.MINOR:
  MINOR goes up when something is ADDED (old plugins still build and run);
  MAJOR goes up when something a plugin may use changes or goes away.
A plugin is accepted when its major equals the engine's and its minor is
not newer. Checked twice: at build time against the manifest's
engine_api (a refused plugin is not compiled; the game reports it), and
at load time against the CW_ENGINE_API the plugin's code was compiled
with (CW_PLUGIN records it), which is what catches a stale native plugin
library. Internal headers (src/, editor/core/) are never part of it.

headers.summary:
cartwheel profiler: named zones on every thread, frame boundaries, GPU pass
times, counters, and Chrome / Perfetto trace files.

  void physics_step(...) {
    CW_PROFILE_SCOPE("physics3d.step");   // a zone until the end of the block
    ...
  }
  CW_PROFILE_COUNTER("render.draw_calls", st.draw_calls); // a per-frame number

Cost. Compiled out (CMake -DCW_PROFILER=OFF, or `#define CW_PROFILE_ENABLED 0`
before including this header): the macros expand to nothing. Compiled in
but off at run time (the default): one relaxed atomic load per zone. On:
two monotonic clock reads and one 32-byte write into the thread's own ring.

What is recorded. Each thread that records a zone (main, every job worker,
the native audio thread) gets its own ring of completed zones, written
without locks. A job chunk run on any thread is a zone named after the zone
that submitted the job ("physics3d.step/job"), so worker time is attributed
to the system that asked for it; chunks under one name that a thread runs
back to back are one zone. Natively the render passes' GPU times
(GL timer queries read back in a batch every 8 frames, WebGPU timestamp
queries) arrive several frames late and
land in a "GPU" lane, laid end to end from the start of their frame's
render: the durations are measured, the positions are not. They are off
unless asked for (cw_profile_gpu): the queries cost CPU time of their own.
In split screen each view's run of a pass is its own entry ("ssao@v1"),
and the pipeline's own GPU work between passes is timed as steps:
"views" (the views laid into the frame) and "resolve" (the multisampled
scene resolved, the depth copies the later passes sample). On WebGPU a
pass is timed whole, with every render three.c records for it (shadow
maps, G-buffers, probe captures).
Carts never issue GPU timer queries, so a cart's trace has no GPU lane.

Turning it on: cw_profile_set_enabled, `profile on` over the debug channel,
CW_PROFILE=1, or a trace request (below). Profiling never changes what the
game simulates: it reads clocks and writes its own buffers only.

Trace files (Chrome trace event JSON: open in ui.perfetto.dev,
chrome://tracing or speedscope):
  - natively, CW_PROFILE_TRACE=out.json [CW_PROFILE_TRACE_FRAMES=120]
    [CW_PROFILE_TRACE_START=0] records frames START.. START+FRAMES-1 and writes
    the file when the last one ends (or at exit, with what was recorded);
  - from any host (carts through romdev too), the debug channel:
    `profile trace <frames>` records that many frames and then answers with
    the trace's size; `profile trace_get [offset]` returns it in pieces
    (tools/cwtrace.mjs does both and writes the file);
  - from code, cw_profile_trace_json.
Other channel requests: profile on|off|status|clear, profile frames [n] (cpu
and wall ms per recorded frame), profile top [frames] [n] (zones by
exclusive time).

headers.summary:
Project settings for games: project.cwproj, read through the project layer
(cartwheel/vfs.h), so a game sees the same file natively (its project
directory or packed assets) and in a cart (its bundled assets, or the
in-memory layer an editor or tool wrote).

The file is `key = value` lines ('#' or ';' start a comment line; values
may be quoted). Keys the engine and editor use:

  name = My Game                      the project's display name
  app = my_game                       the project's cw_add_app target
  main_scene = main.cwscene
  layer_names_2d / layer_names_3d / gravity_2d / gravity_3d /
  pixels_per_meter / substeps         physics (cartwheel/physics_nodes.h)
  input.<action> = key:space, pad:south   the input map: one action per key,
                                      the cw_input_load_bindings line format
  render.width / render.height        logical resolution (a cart's declared size)
  render.msaa = 4                     default framebuffer samples (native)
  render.vsync = true                 native only
  render.fixed_hz = 60                simulation ticks per second
  export.<preset>.platform / .output / ...   export presets (tools/cwexport)
  net.domains = play.example.com      hosts the cart may dial (wc_peer_open's
                                      manifest grant; read by cw_add_app at build)
Editor and tool keys (the engine itself never reads them):
  scenes = levels/a.cwscene, ...     scenes the editor lists besides main_scene
  sources = src, game.c               C files and directories (the editor's
                                      code view and other tools)
  build / game_module                 the editor's build command and hot module
  game_exe / game_cart                written by tools/cwproject.mjs after a
                                      build: what the editor's Play launches

Every function here may be called from cw_main (before init): the file is
read on first use and cached.

headers.summary:
cartwheel/quality.h: graphics settings, the presets that set them, and
the automatic choice.

Each setting is something the player can pick on its own; a preset picks
them all:

                    Low       Medium    High (default)  Ultra
  resolution        67%       75%       100%            100%
  ambient occl.     off       on        on              on
  shadows           Low       Medium    High            Ultra
  anti-aliasing     FXAA      FXAA      SMAA            SMAA
  effects detail    Low       Medium    High            Ultra

Resolution: the 3D scene (and its post) renders at that share of the
output's size and is scaled up with a filter (Catmull-Rom); the 2D window
passes (HUD, menus, text) draw at the output's full size over it. It is the
biggest lever: GPU time of the scene and its post goes with its pixel
count. It applies on top of cw_app_desc.render_scale (the output size);
an app with pixel_scale draws at its own size and ignores it.

Ambient occlusion: GTAO as the scene's PostProcess asks for it (On) or
none (Off); its sample count follows effects detail.

Shadows: Low (maps of 1024 at most, hard PCF), Medium (1024 at most,
soft), High (as the lights ask, soft), Ultra (twice that, up to 4096,
soft).

Anti-aliasing: Off, FXAA, or SMAA (as the PostProcess asks: a scene that
asks for FXAA or none keeps it). The scene's MSAA (PostProcess msaa) is the
game's and stays on every preset, on GL and WebGPU alike (4x WebGPU, as
GL at 4); Off turns it off too.

Effects detail (Low, Medium, High, Ultra): the share of GPU particles
drawn (0.4, 0.7, 1, 1), the density games thin their instancing by (0.35,
0.65, 1, 1: grass, crowd, scatter), the bloom chain (3, 5 levels, as
authored), GTAO's samples (1 slice of 4 steps, 1 of 4, as authored, 3
slices of 8 steps), the LOD error budget (x2, x1.5, x1, x1: coarser
meshes sooner), the clustered lights one cluster keeps (x0.375, x0.5,
x1, x1 of LightingSettings.max_per_cluster: 24, 32, 64, 64 by default;
cw_quality_scale("lights"), cartwheel/lighting.h) and the volumetric fog
grid (cartwheel/environment.h: 64 x 32, 96 x 48, 160 x 64, 240 x 96 cells
across x slices), the distortion buffer (cartwheel/explosions.h: half the
frame on Low and Medium, the whole frame on High and Ultra;
cw_quality_scale("distortion")), colour fringing on bent edges (High and
Ultra: "dispersion"), the share of the explosion light pool in use
(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1: "flash_lights") and skin shading (Medium and up:
"skin", cartwheel/skin_shading.h; Low draws skin as plain PBR).

"As authored" is what the scene's PostProcess / lights ask for: High
draws exactly what the game would without this module.

Game settings: a game adds its own render-only levers (cw_quality_lever_add:
a cheaper material at distance, say) with the value each preset picks;
they show in the graphics menu after the engine's, and are saved with them.

Density: games read cw_quality_scale("grass"), ("crowd"), ("scatter") or
the shorthand cw_quality_density() and thin their instancing; set a change
callback to re-thin when a setting changes. Particles: the engine draws
cw_quality_scale("particles") of every GPU particle system's particles
(they are all still simulated, so counts and seeds agree).

The player picks a preset, Auto, or each setting (the graphics menu,
cartwheel/quality_menu.h, or the game shell's settings); changing one
setting shows the preset as "Custom". Persist the choice in the game's
save data (cw_quality_saved / cw_quality_restore below).

Auto: the engine picks, and holds the frame's cost under a budget. While
the game says it is in play (cw_quality_auto_measure(true) every frame) it
averages the cost: the GPU time of the frame's passes where the host
times them cheaply (native WebGPU's timestamps), else the frame-to-frame
time (GL, a cart: a frame the GPU cannot finish in time arrives late). After a couple of
seconds over budget it steps down one level of its ladder:

  High 100%, High 85%, Medium 75%, Medium 67%, Low 67%, Low 60%, Low 50%

(resolution first: it costs the picture least for what it saves; a game
that asks for cw_quality_full_resolution gets High, Medium, Low at 100%). Where
it measures GPU time it also steps back up when the cost has stayed well
under budget, never into a level that was over it in this run. A game
makes Auto the starting choice with cw_quality_auto(true, budget); the
player can always pick it. The level it reached is saved, so the next run
starts there.

Determinism: a deterministic run (a test) starts at High whatever the
save holds, with Auto off, so every host draws the same frame; a choice
made in it (from the menus, by input every host replays alike) applies.
Nothing here reaches the simulation.

The preset now: the one picked, Auto's current level, or (Custom) the
preset the settings were last set from.

Choose a preset (every setting). user = true: the player chose it (Auto
stops); false: the game or a tool did (Auto, when on, may still change
it). Calls the change callback.

Settings shown: the engine's, then the game's levers (ids
CW_GFX_ENGINE_COUNT + i, in the order they were added).

The player sets one (value clamped): the preset becomes Custom unless the
settings now match one, and Auto stops.

functions.signature: bool cw_quality_scope_push(const char *name, const int8_t caps[CW_GFX_ENGINE_COUNT])
functions.doc:
A scene or mode that does not need everything (a 2D mini-game, a scene with no use for ambient occlusion) caps
settings for as long as it is on screen: caps[CW_GFX_RESOLUTION ... CW_GFX_EFFECTS] each hold the highest value
allowed (-1 leaves that setting alone). A scope only ever LOWERS what the player chose, so a player on Low
stays on Low and the menu still shows the player's choice. Scopes nest (four at most); the lowest cap wins.
Render-only, like the rest of this header: call between frames. Returns false when it is not opened.

functions.signature: int cw_quality_lever_add(const char *name, const char *const *values, int value_count, const uint8_t preset[CW_QUALITY_COUNT])
