A game's own render-only setting (at most CW_GFX_MAX_LEVERS, each with up
to CW_GFX_LEVER_MAX_VALUES values, cheapest first): its name, its values'
labels (kept by pointer: static strings) and the value each preset picks
(preset[CW_QUALITY_LOW] ...). Call in init, before cw_quality_restore (the
saved value applies to it). Returns its setting id (for cw_gfx_get), -1
when full.

functions.name: cw_quality_scale
functions.doc:
A scale for a named knob, from effects detail: "particles", "density",
"grass", "crowd", "scatter" (the last three are density), "hrtf_voices"
(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1: the audio mixer's HRTF voice limit, cartwheel/audio.h),
1 for any other name.

functions.name: cw_quality_density
functions.doc: cw_quality_scale("density")

functions.name: cw_quality_count
functions.doc: n scaled by a knob, at least 1 when n > 0

functions.name: cw_quality_on_change
functions.doc: the change callback (NULL removes it)

functions.name: cw_quality_auto
functions.doc:
on: Auto is the choice until the player picks something else (a save
with a choice in it wins). budget_ms <= 0 keeps the default: 19 ms of
frame time (a 60 Hz display that keeps missing frames), or three quarters
of it of GPU time where the GPU is timed. Off in a deterministic run.

functions.name: cw_quality_auto_measure
functions.doc: every frame: true while the frame time means something

functions.name: cw_quality_full_resolution
functions.doc:
Full resolution (opt in; off by default): the game always draws its 3D at
the output's size. Every preset keeps Resolution at 100% (Low and Medium
keep their other settings), and Auto's ladder drops its resolution steps:
High, Medium, Low, each at 100%. Only the player picking a resolution in
the graphics menu changes it. For a game whose look depends on full-size
pixels, or a host that must never upscale. Call in init, before
cw_quality_restore.

functions.name: cw_quality_is_auto
functions.doc: Auto is choosing (not a test run)

functions.name: cw_quality_is_custom
functions.doc: the settings match no preset (and Auto is off)

functions.name: cw_quality_auto_cost
functions.doc:
Auto's measured cost in ms (averaged; GPU time or frame time, as above),
0 before it has measured

functions.name: cw_quality_cycle
functions.doc:
The next choice in Low, Medium, High, Ultra, Auto, Low... (a player's
choice; from Custom, the preset after the one it came from).
Render-only: call it from update or event handling, never from the
fixed-step simulation. The frame's raw presses (cw_input_raw:
keys_pressed, pads[].pressed, mouse_pressed) hold for the whole frame, so
update sees them as the ticks do.

functions.name: cw_quality_cycle_back
functions.doc: the previous choice in that order

functions.name: cw_quality_label
functions.doc: "Low", "Medium", "High", "Ultra", "Auto" or "Custom": what a settings entry shows

functions.name: cw_render_res_label
functions.doc:
The render resolution as a graphics menu shows it: "<lines>p" of the
scene's render size (cw_render_size, the resolution setting applied),
e.g. "720p", "1080p". The output's size is the host's (RetroArch: Quick
Menu > Core Options > Internal Resolution).

functions.name: cw_quality_saved
functions.doc:
Save data: a word the game keeps in its save (0 = none chosen). It holds
the choice (a preset, Auto and the level it reached, or every setting of a
Custom choice, the game's levers too); cw_quality_restore applies it (at
init, after the save loaded and the levers were added; not in a
deterministic run). It fits in 13 bits
(two bytes) for a game with no levers, 21 bits (three bytes) with four.
A byte 1..4 from an older save is still a preset.

functions.name: cw_quality_restore
functions.doc: apply a cw_quality_saved word (0 = none chosen)

types.name: cw_quality

Called after any setting changes (a preset, a setting, an Auto step), on

Drive it from the game's own mapping: dy -1 / +1 up / down, dx -1 / +1

headers.summary:
cartwheel ragdolls: a skeleton (cartwheel/ik.h cw_pose) turned into Box3D
bodies and joints, seeded from the current pose, and written back onto the
pose so the skinned mesh follows the bodies.

A ragdoll is a list of parts. Each part is one bone (a capsule from the
bone's origin to a tip: a child bone's origin or an offset), hung from the
nearest ancestor bone that is also a part by a joint with limits:
  BALL   a cone around the bone's rest direction (relative to its parent
         part) and a twist range about the bone (shoulders, hips, neck,
         spine)
  HINGE  one axis (knees, elbows) with an angle range; 0 is the rest pose
Limits are measured from the REST pose (cw_pose rest_*), so a ragdoll
made from any animated pose keeps the same anatomy. Bones that are not
parts (fingers, face, twist bones) keep whatever local transform the pose
has, so they ride along with their part.

Typical use (a character knocked down; see docs/guides/animation.md
"Ragdolls"):
  on the knockdown: r = cw_ragdoll_create(world, &def, &pose, &model_to_world);
                    cw_ragdoll_set_velocity(r, v, spin); cw_ragdoll_apply_impulse(...)
  each tick:        cw_world3d_step(world, dt);
                    cw_pose_capture(&pose);          the animated pose
                    cw_ragdoll_blend_pose(r, &pose, &model_to_world, w);  w = 1 while limp
                    cw_pose_flush(&pose);
  to get up:        when cw_ragdoll_resting(): pick a get-up clip by
                    cw_ragdoll_axis (face up or down), play it, and ramp
                    w from 1 to 0 over a few tenths of a second; then
                    cw_ragdoll_destroy(r).

The ragdoll lives in the cw_world3d it was made in and collides with
whatever is there (ground, props). Its own parts never collide with each
other (one negative group per ragdoll unless def.group says otherwise).

DETERMINISM. Box3D steps are bit-identical across hosts for the same
inputs, and everything here is + - * / sqrt on floats, so a ragdoll made
from the same pose and impulses lands the same way on every host
(cw_ragdoll_hash folds every body transform: a cross-host test compares
it). Keep ragdolls out of game rules anyway when the rules run on a fixed
tick of their own: treat them as presentation.

COST: a part is one body, one capsule and one joint: a 14 part humanoid is
about the cost of 14 boxes in a stack while it moves; resting ragdolls
fall asleep (no cost). docs/guides/animation.md has measured numbers.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_default_def
functions.doc: The defaults noted above, with parts/count from the arguments.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_create
functions.signature: cw_ragdoll *cw_ragdoll_create(cw_world3d w, const cw_ragdoll_def *def, const cw_pose *pose, const t3_mat4 *model_to_world)
functions.doc:
Bodies and joints for every part in `w`, placed where the pose's bones are
(its current model transforms: call cw_pose_capture or
cw_pose_update_model first) under `model_to_world` (rotation, translation
and a uniform scale). NULL (logged) when a part's bone or tip is missing
from the pose or the world is invalid. Velocities start at zero.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_destroy
functions.doc: Removes the bodies and joints and frees the ragdoll. NULL is fine.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_part_count
functions.doc: the number of parts (0 for NULL)

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_find
functions.doc: part index of a bone name, -1 when it is not a part

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_body
functions.doc:
the part's physics body (cartwheel/physics3d.h), to read its velocity or
push it directly; a zero handle for a part out of range or a NULL ragdoll

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_part_transform
functions.doc: the part's world transform (its bone's origin and rotation)

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_axis
functions.signature: t3_vec3 cw_ragdoll_axis(const cw_ragdoll *r, int part, t3_vec3 rest_model_dir)
functions.doc:
A model-space direction at REST (e.g. (0,0,1): the way the chest faced in
the bind pose) as it points now in world space, carried by the part.
Face up or face down: the chest's rest forward against world up.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_set_velocity
functions.signature: void cw_ragdoll_set_velocity(cw_ragdoll *r, t3_vec3 v, t3_vec3 angular)
functions.doc:
Every part moves with linear velocity v plus a spin `angular` (rad/s,
world) about the root part: the whole body carried by a blow.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_apply_impulse
functions.signature: int cw_ragdoll_apply_impulse(cw_ragdoll *r, int part, t3_vec3 impulse, t3_vec3 point)
functions.doc:
An impulse (N*s) at a world point on one part; part < 0: the part whose
capsule is nearest the point. Returns the part hit.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_apply_force
functions.doc:
A force (N) at the root part's centre for this step (keep a ragdoll near a
point: a tether, wind).

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_write_pose
functions.signature: void cw_ragdoll_write_pose(const cw_ragdoll *r, cw_pose *pose, const t3_mat4 *model_to_world)
functions.doc:
Write the bodies into the pose: every part bone gets the model rotation of
its body, the root part's bone also its position; other bones keep their
local transforms. Model transforms are updated; flush to show it.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_blend_pose
functions.signature: void cw_ragdoll_blend_pose(cw_ragdoll *r, cw_pose *pose, const t3_mat4 *model_to_world, float w)
functions.doc:
Blend the pose toward the ragdoll by w (0 = the pose as it is, 1 = the
ragdoll): local translations lerp, rotations slerp, per bone. Ramping w
down while a get-up clip plays hands the body from physics back to
animation without a pop. Call it every tick on the freshly captured pose
(w 0 included) until the ragdoll is destroyed: a part bone that no clip
writes would otherwise keep the last ragdoll angle, so a bone that still
holds exactly what the previous call left gets back the local transform
it had when the ragdoll was made.

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_resting
functions.doc: true when every part moves slower than `speed` (m/s, and rad/s for spin)

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_max_speed
functions.doc: the largest speed of any part (m/s)

functions.name: cw_ragdoll_joint_angle
cw_ragdoll_hash
functions.doc: FNV-1a over every body's position and rotation bits, folded into h

types.name: cw_ragdoll_joint_kind
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_RAGDOLL_BALL, CW_RAGDOLL_HINGE } cw_ragdoll_joint_kind;

types.name: cw_ragdoll_part
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_ragdoll_part {
  const char *bone;            /* the bone this body drives */
  const char *tip;             /* the capsule ends at this bone's origin (usually a child); NULL: tip_offset */
  const char *attach;          /* hang from this part (a bone name) instead of the nearest part above it in the skeleton:
                                * for bones outside the chain they belong to (an IK rig's feet under the root); the bone's
                                * position is written as well as its rotation */
  t3_vec3 tip_offset;          /* model-space offset from the bone's origin at REST, when tip is NULL */
  float radius;                /* capsule radius in world metres */
  float density_scale;         /* times def.density; 0 = 1 */
  cw_ragdoll_joint_kind joint; /* how it hangs from its parent part (ignored for the root part) */
  float swing;                 /* BALL: cone half angle, radians (0: no cone limit) */
  float lower, upper;          /* BALL: twist about the bone; HINGE: angle about axis (radians, 0 = rest) */
  t3_vec3 axis;                /* HINGE: the hinge axis in model space at rest (e.g. (1,0,0) for a knee) */
} cw_ragdoll_part;

types.name: cw_ragdoll_def
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_ragdoll_def {
  const cw_ragdoll_part *parts; /* parents before children is not required; a part's parent is found by bone */
  int count;                    /* up to CW_RAGDOLL_MAX_PARTS */
  float density;                /* kg/m^3 of the capsules: 1000 (water: a human's mass from body-sized capsules) */
  float friction;               /* contact friction: 0.7 */
  float restitution;            /* bounce: 0.05 */
  float joint_friction;         /* N*m resisting every joint's motion (a motor at zero speed): 2; 0 = limp */
  float linear_damping, angular_damping; /* 0.05, 0.6 */
  int layer;                    /* collision layer of every part: 0 */
  uint32_t mask;                /* layers the parts collide with: all */
  int group;                    /* 0: a fresh negative group per ragdoll (no self collision) */
} cw_ragdoll_def;

types.name: cw_ragdoll
types.decl: typedef struct cw_ragdoll cw_ragdoll;

headers.summary:
cartwheel remote: the EDITOR side of play-in-editor.

Launches a game under edit and talks to it over the debug channel
(cartwheel/debug.h), the same text requests and JSON replies romdev's
wasm({op:'command'}) uses. The game never runs in the editor's address
space, so a crashing game cannot take the editor down: the editor sees the
crash as a state change and relaunches.

Transports (same API, same requests):
  CW_REMOTE_NATIVE  the game executable as a child process. The editor
                    makes a socketpair; the child inherits one end and gets
                    CW_REMOTE=fd:N (the channel turns on even without
                    .debug). Exits and crashes (signals) are detected with
                    waitpid; the child's stdout/stderr come back as log
                    lines. Linux only: on Linux the child also dies with
                    the editor (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, plus EOF on the socket
                    quits it); macOS works the same but without the
                    death signal; Windows is not implemented yet.
  CW_REMOTE_ROMDEV  the game's .wasc in romdev (HTTP to its tool route,
                    default http://127.0.0.1:7331, one session per
                    cw_remote): loadMedia, then each request is
                    wasm({op:'command'}). romdev runs a cart only when told,
                    so a worker thread keeps the game's frames flowing at
                    60 per wall-clock second while it is not paused. A
                    wasm trap or an evicted host is reported as a crash /
                    exit like a native one.
An editor that is itself a CART has no transport: a cart cannot open a
socket or spawn anything, and wasmcart's wc_peer_* (the only network ABI)
needs a host that registers a peer to the game, which no host does today
(romdev has no wc_peer support). cw_remote_launch fails there and says so.

Threading: one cw_remote belongs to one thread (the editor's frame loop);
the romdev transport's worker is internal.

Use from a frame loop:

  cw_remote *g = cw_remote_launch(&(cw_remote_desc){ .transport = CW_REMOTE_NATIVE,
                                                     .exe = "build/native/games/action2d",
                                                     .start_paused = true });
  cw_remote_send(g, "tree", 0, on_tree, ui);     // async; on_tree runs inside pump
  ... every frame: cw_remote_pump(g);
  if (cw_remote_state_of(g) == CW_REMOTE_CRASHED) show(cw_remote_status(g)), cw_remote_relaunch(g);

The request language is the debug channel's (`help` lists a game's
commands). The play-in-editor set: status, pause [1|0], resume,
step <ticks>, tree [node] [depth], node <node>, changes <revision>,
get <node> <prop...>, set <node> <prop> <value>, props, methods, call,
emit, spawn, free, change_scene, reload_scene, reload <res path...>,
screenshot <world|ui|debug|all> [scale] + screenshot_get, record ...,
stats, phys, quit. Nodes are addressed as #uid (stable) or by path.

functions.name: cw_remote_launch
functions.doc:
Launch the game. Returns NULL only when d is unusable (no exe / cart) or
on a cart build; a game that fails to start comes back in state FAILED
with the reason in cw_remote_status. Blocks until the game answers
(`status`) or launch_timeout_ms passes. cw_remote_last_error() explains a
NULL.

functions.name: cw_remote_last_error
functions.doc: why the last cw_remote_launch returned NULL

functions.name: cw_remote_close
functions.doc:
Stop the game (quit request, then a kill after a moment) and free r.
Pending requests complete with an error.

functions.name: cw_remote_relaunch
functions.doc:
Stop the game if it still runs and start it again from the same desc.
Requests in flight fail. true when the new game answers.

functions.name: cw_remote_stop
functions.doc: Stop the game, keep r (state CLOSED; relaunch restarts it).

functions.name: cw_remote_kill
functions.doc:
Kill the game without asking (SIGKILL natively; romdev: the host is shut
down). For crash-isolation tests; the state becomes CRASHED.

functions.name: cw_remote_state_of
functions.doc: where the game is; pump updates it

functions.name: cw_remote_state_name
functions.doc: "running", "crashed", ...

functions.name: cw_remote_status
functions.doc:
One line on the game's state: "running (pid 1234)", "crashed: signal 11
(SIGSEGV)", "exited with code 0", "romdev: unreachable (wasm trap)", ...

functions.name: cw_remote_pid
functions.doc: native child pid, 0 otherwise

functions.name: cw_remote_launch_count
functions.doc: 1 after launch, +1 per relaunch

functions.name: cw_remote_send
functions.signature: uint32_t cw_remote_send(cw_remote *r, const char *request, int timeout_ms, cw_remote_cb cb, void *user)
functions.doc:
Queue a request (debug-channel text, under 4 KiB for romdev). Returns its
id (> 0), or 0 when the game is not running (cb is not called then).
timeout_ms 0 = the desc's default. cb (may be NULL) runs inside
cw_remote_pump / cw_remote_wait on the calling thread; the reply's
strings are valid during the callback only.

functions.name: cw_remote_pump
functions.doc:
Deliver what has arrived: replies (callbacks), timeouts, exits/crashes,
log lines. Never blocks. Returns how many replies it delivered. Call once
per editor frame.

functions.name: cw_remote_wait
functions.signature: bool cw_remote_wait(cw_remote *r, uint32_t id, int timeout_ms)
functions.doc:
Pump until request `id` completes or timeout_ms passes. true when it
completed (successfully or not: the callback or cw_remote_take says).

functions.name: cw_remote_call
functions.signature: char *cw_remote_call(cw_remote *r, const char *request, int timeout_ms, char **error_out)
functions.doc:
Blocking convenience (tools, tests): send, wait, return the reply
JSON (malloc'd; free it) or NULL with the reason in *error_out (malloc'd,

headers.summary:
cartwheel 2D renderer: a batched, immediate-mode-style submission API.

Every frame, between cw_r2d_begin() and cw_r2d_end(), the game submits
sprites, shapes, text, tilemaps and lights into canvas LAYERS. Nothing is
drawn while submitting: cw_r2d_end() sorts what was submitted (layer, then
z, then y when the layer y-sorts, then submission order; the sort is
stable), cuts it into batches and draws. A batch only ends where the GL
state has to change: a different texture ARRAY, blend mode, clip rect or
shader (tilemaps, lit layers). Every texture lives in a GL_TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY
page, so sprites from many atlas pages share one draw, and solid shapes,
SDF text and additive sprites batch with textured sprites (the fragment
shader branches on a per-vertex mode). A typical frame is a handful of
draws.

Coordinates: canvas pixels, origin top-left, y down. Angles in radians,
positive = clockwise on screen. Colours are straight (not premultiplied)
0..1 floats; the renderer premultiplies internally. All textures are stored
premultiplied, and blending is premultiplied-alpha throughout.

GL: OpenGL ES 3.0 / WebGL2 through cartwheel/gl.h, the same code natively
and in carts. The renderer needs a current context (call from init()
onward) and owns no context state between passes: each cw_r2d_end() sets
everything it uses (framebuffer, viewport, program, VAO, blend, scissor,
stencil, depth and cull off, texture unit 0..2) and leaves those changed.
Sharing the context with three.c: call t3_renderer_reset_bindings(r)
after any 2D pass and before the next t3_renderer_render(), so three.c's
GL state cache matches GL again (the 2D renderer never touches three.c's
programs, so the cheaper reset is enough). Draw three.c INTO a 2D render
target with t3_renderer_set_framebuffer(r, cw_target_fbo(rt)) plus
t3_renderer_set_size(r, w, h); the target then draws as a sprite.

Costs: submission is O(vertices) on the calling thread (cw_r2d_sprites
spreads big arrays over the job pool); cw_r2d_end() is one radix sort when
the submission is not already in order, one upload per stream (vertices,
indices; orphaned each pass, a ring of 3 buffers), and one draw call per
batch. Memory is tagged CW_MEM_RENDER2D.

Threads: call everything from the main (GL) thread.

functions.name: cw_font_preload_range
functions.signature: void cw_font_preload_range(cw_font f, uint32_t first, uint32_t last)
functions.doc:
Prepare glyphs during init/warmup, on the main rendering thread. These
populate the same font/atlas caches as drawing; they submit no draw commands.
Repeated calls reuse cached glyphs. Work and atlas memory move to loading;
preload only the repertoire needed by the game/current locale.
SDF caches serve every display size. Bitmap caches use the font's bake size.
Call again after changing fallback fonts/locales. Null/stale fonts are no-ops.
Range is inclusive, limited to Unicode scalar values (surrogates skipped).
Reversed ranges or first > U+10FFFF are no-ops; last is clamped to U+10FFFF.
English UI: cw_font_preload_range(font, 32, 126).
Use text for localized strings: it also prepares contextual shaped glyphs;
a range alone cannot anticipate all ligatures/contextual forms. NULL text
is a no-op. Layout at draw time still honors the requested style.

types.doc:
── render targets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A target is a standalone texture you can draw into (cw_r2d_begin with
.target) and then draw as a sprite. Content follows GL's orientation
(row 0 = bottom); the renderer flips it back when sampling, so a target
drawn as a sprite shows what was drawn into it upright, whether a 2D pass
or three.c filled it.

A plain value the game owns. The view maps world -> canvas pixels:
  screen = anchor + offset + R(-rotation) * ((world - position*parallax) * zoom)
where anchor is the viewport's centre (or its top-left corner with
anchor_top_left). Zero-initialized fields mean zoom 1, no rotation.

── arbitrary geometry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
uv is 0..1 over the texture's whole rect (past 1 only on repeat
textures). A null texture draws vertex colours.
types.decl: typedef struct cw_vertex2d { cw_vec2 pos, uv; cw_color color; } cw_vertex2d;

types.name: cw_font_mode
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_FONT_SDF, CW_FONT_BITMAP } cw_font_mode;

types.name: cw_font_desc
cw_text_align
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_ALIGN_LEFT, CW_ALIGN_CENTER, CW_ALIGN_RIGHT } cw_text_align;

types.name: cw_text_dir
types.doc:
Paragraph direction for bidi text (complex path only): AUTO takes the
first strong character's direction.
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_TEXT_DIR_AUTO, CW_TEXT_DIR_LTR, CW_TEXT_DIR_RTL } cw_text_dir;

types.name: cw_text_style
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_text_style {
  float size;           /* pixel size of the em (0 = the font's bake size) */
  cw_color color;       /* {0,0,0,0} = white */
  float wrap_width;     /* 0 = no wrapping */
  cw_text_align align;  /* within wrap_width, or within the widest line when not wrapping */
  float line_spacing;   /* multiple of the font's line height (0 = 1) */
  float letter_spacing; /* extra pixels after every glyph */
  int32_t direction;    /* cw_text_dir (complex-script text only) */
  /* Outline and drop shadow, drawn under the text from the same layout (one
   * submission, batched with it). SDF fonts grow and soften the glyphs in
   * the shader: a round outline of any width up to the font's distance range
   * (sdf_padding baked px at bake_size: 6 at 48 = 12.5% of the size by
   * default; a wider one clamps with a warning naming the padding to load the
   * font with). Bitmap fonts stamp the glyphs at every whole-pixel offset
   * within the width (softness ignored). Widths in px at this size. */
  float outline_width;      /* 0 = none */
  cw_color outline_color;   /* {0,0,0,0} = opaque black */
  cw_color shadow_color;    /* alpha 0 = no shadow */
  cw_vec2 shadow_offset;    /* px */
  float shadow_spread;      /* px the shadow grows round the glyphs */
  float shadow_softness;    /* px of blur at the shadow's edge (SDF) */
} cw_text_style;

types.name: cw_text_metrics
cw_tilemap_desc
cw_light2d
types.doc:
── 2D lights ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Layers marked lit are drawn into an offscreen colour buffer (and, when a
texture with a normal map was drawn, a normal buffer), then composited as
colour * light. The light buffer starts at the pass's ambient colour and
each light adds itself (additive, radial falloff, one quad). Shadows are
analytic: each occluder edge facing away from the light is extruded away
from it into the stencil buffer, and the light is masked by it (hard
shadows, exact at any resolution; 2 draws per shadowed light). The light
buffer is RGBA8 storing light/2, so lights can overbright up to 2x.

Lights and occluders are submitted into the current layer (its camera
places them) and affect the run of consecutive lit layers they are in.

types.name: cw_r2d_stats
types.doc:
── stats ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Totals for the current frame (reset by the first cw_r2d_begin of each
engine frame), complete once the frame's last pass ended.

macros.name: CW_R2D_MAX_LAYERS
macros.doc:
── canvas layers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CW_R2D_MAX_LAYERS layers, drawn in index order (0 first). Each has its own
camera, so a world layer and a HUD layer coexist; settings persist across
passes and frames (a scene tree's canvas draw puts back those it used).
Layer 0 with no camera is the default: screen space.

macros.name: CW_TILE_CHUNK
macros.doc:
── tilemaps ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Grid maps in chunks of CW_TILE_CHUNK x CW_TILE_CHUNK tiles per layer; each
chunk is static geometry in its own buffer, rebuilt only when one of its
cells is edited. Drawing culls chunks to the layer's view; each map layer
is one draw per visible chunk, ordered with everything else by the canvas
layer and z it was submitted at. Animated tiles cycle in the vertex shader
from the pass time: no rebuilds.

macros.name: CW_TILE_FLIP_X
macros.doc:
Cell value: tile id + 1 in the low 24 bits (0 = empty), transform flags in
the high bits (Tiled's convention, so Tiled maps load unchanged).

headers.summary:
3D rendering for the scene tree: each tree owns a three.c scene and
renderer; Node3D objects attach under it, and the 3D render node types
(Camera3D, MeshInstance3D, lights, WorldEnvironment) configure it.

Node types registered here:
  Camera3D          fov, near, far, current (the first current camera renders)
Every node type's properties (type, default, doc) are in docs/nodes.json and
answer to the debug channel: `types`, `props <path>`.

Conventions: Y is up, -Z is forward. Cameras look down their -Z. Lights
(directional, spot) shine down their -Z, NOT at the origin as three.js's
default target does: aim them with rotation or cw_node3d_look_at (which
points -Z at the target for every Node3D).

  MeshInstance3D    primitive (NONE, BOX, SPHERE, PLANE, CYLINDER) with size:
                    BOX x/y/z extents; SPHERE size.x = diameter; CYLINDER
                    size.x = diameter along Y, size.y = height; PLANE x by z,
                    facing +Y. Also color,
                    metalness, roughness, emissive, cast_shadow, receive_shadow,
                    mesh (a resource uid, when a mesh resource is set it wins)
  DirectionalLight3D, OmniLight3D, SpotLight3D   color, energy, shadow, range...;
                    energy is 0 to 100000 (the sun's real illuminance is
                    about 100000 lux); a value outside is clamped, and the
                    first clamp of a light logs a warning
                    a directional shadow covers shadow_extent metres around
                    the light (move the light with the player for sharp
                    shadows over a big level), shadow_bias / shadow_normal_bias
  WorldEnvironment  background, ambient color/energy, fog (linear colours;
                    tone curve + exposure live in PostProcess)
  PostProcess       the render pipeline's settings (pipeline.h): HDR,
                    MSAA, exposure, tone curve,
                    bloom, SSAO, TAA, FXAA/SMAA, LUT, lens effects
  ProceduralSky, HeightFog   sky / day-night, fog (environment.h)
  LightmapGI        baked lightmaps and SH probes (lightmap.h)
  MeshInstance3D also carries visibility properties (static, lod_bias,
                    visibility_range, occlusion_cull, impostor...): see
                    visibility.h (VisibilityManager, Room3D, Portal3D).
                    Primitives are unit shapes shared per tree and scaled
                    to `size`, so same-shaped meshes instance.
Effects node types live in particles.h (GPUParticles3D, GPUParticles2D,
ParticleAttractor3D, ParticleCollider3D, Trail3D) and decals.h (Decal3D).

Which lights three.c draws and which the engine clusters: the tree's
lighting mode (cartwheel/lighting.h, a LightingSettings node). FORWARD,
the default, leaves every light to three.c; CLUSTERED shades shadowless
omni and spot lights through r187 ClusteredLighting's clusters, hundreds
at a time.

Drawing goes through the tree's render pipeline (pipeline.h), as three.js
r187 draws: linear colours, physical light units, linear HDR.

functions.name: cw_mesh3d_set_procedural
functions.doc:
Attach a procedural mesh to a MeshInstance3D for visibility/BVH support.
Retains mesh as a child of the node; preserves its local transform, materials
and shadow flags. While attached, primitive/resource/look properties are
ignored. NULL restores property-driven geometry. No automatic LOD chain is
inferred. Returns false for another node type or an already-parented mesh.

functions.name: cw_geometry_optimize_vertex_cache
functions.doc:
Reorder an indexed geometry's triangles for the GPU's post-transform vertex cache (meshoptimizer's
optimizeVertexCache, Forsyth-style): the same triangles and vertices, an order in which each vertex is
shaded fewer times. Meshes exported in modelling order often run the vertex shader two or three times a
vertex; for a crowd of thousands of instanced characters that is most of its vertex cost. Opaque meshes draw
the same picture (depth decides what shows; only exact depth ties between a mesh's own triangles can
differ); a transparent mesh drawn without sorting changes its blend order. Call once after building the
geometry, before its first draw. acmr_before / acmr_after (either may be NULL): vertices shaded per triangle
for a 16-entry cache, before and after (report only). false (nothing changed) without an index or with an
index past the vertices. Opt in: nothing calls it for you.

functions.name: cw_render3d_scene
functions.doc: The tree's three.c scene, created on first use and owned by the tree (freed with it).

functions.name: cw_render3d_renderer
functions.doc: NULL before the first draw

functions.name: cw_render3d_window_renderer
functions.doc:
A three.c renderer an app drives itself (t3_renderer_render, no scene
tree), on whichever GPU API this run uses: t3_renderer_new, plus three.c's
WebGPU backend on a WebGPU run (a dual cart must not touch GL once the
host selected WebGPU). Draw to the window with cw_render3d_window_target.

functions.name: cw_render3d_texture_target
functions.doc:
Before a t3_renderer_render into a 2D render target (cw_target_create with
depth; null handle = the window, as cw_render3d_window_target): the target
then draws as a sprite the right way up, on GL and WebGPU. Size the renderer
to the target first (t3_renderer_set_size) and back to the window after.

functions.name: cw_render3d_window_target
functions.doc:
Before each t3_renderer_render of a cw_render3d_window_renderer that draws
to the window: point it at this frame's window (the frame texture on
WebGPU; nothing to do on GL, where it draws to the default framebuffer).

functions.name: cw_render3d_draw
functions.signature: bool cw_render3d_draw(cw_tree *t, int w, int h)
functions.doc:
Render the tree's 3D scene through its current camera into the bound
framebuffer (or the renderer's), w x h pixels. Returns false (and creates
nothing) when the tree has no current Camera3D.

functions.name: cw_render3d_prepare
functions.doc:
What cw_render3d_draw does before it renders: create or resize the
renderer to w x h and update the current camera's projection. Returns the
camera to render with, NULL (creating nothing) when the tree has no
current Camera3D. The render pipeline (pipeline.h) calls this, then
renders into its own targets.

functions.name: cw_render3d_camera
functions.doc: explicit camera if still valid, else the first current Camera3D (O(nodes) walk); null when none

functions.name: cw_render3d_set_camera
functions.doc: overrides the current Camera3D; a null handle reverts to the search

functions.name: cw_camera3d_t3
functions.doc: owned by the node; NULL when not a Camera3D

functions.name: cw_render3d_get_stats
functions.doc:
renderer counters from the last draw; zeroed before the first render.
cpu_ms: CPU milliseconds the last frame spent issuing its 3D (the render
pipeline from its start to the overlay phase, or cw_render3d_draw):
submission only, the GPU is not waited for.

types.name: cw_render3d_stats

headers.summary:
cartwheel resources: shared, immutable-at-runtime data (textures, meshes,
materials, glTF scenes, audio clips, fonts, JSON/text blobs, and whatever
other modules register) loaded once and shared by everyone who asks.

Addressing. A resource has three names:
  - a handle (cw_res): generational, what code holds; stale reads as NULL;
  - a path: "res://models/duck.glb" or "models/duck.glb" (the same thing),
    relative to the asset root (a .cwpak natively, the cart bundle in a
    cart). Files read through the project layer first (cartwheel/vfs.h:
    a native project directory, files written or imported into memory),
    so an editor's project and a cart's imported files load too. A '#' addresses a sub-resource of a loaded file:
      "models/duck.glb#mesh/0/1"   mesh 0, primitive 1 (a cw_mesh)
      "models/duck.glb#material/2" glTF material 2 (a t3_material)
      "models/duck.glb#texture/0"  glTF texture 0 (a t3_texture)
  - a UID: a stable 64-bit id that survives renames. cwpack writes
    "res.index" (uid, type, path per line) into every pack; a file's UID
    comes from its .cwimport sidecar (uid=0x...), else the hash of its path
    (cw_res_path_uid).

Lifetime. Every load returns a NEW reference (refcount + 1); release it with
cw_res_release. Loading a path that is already loaded (or still loading)
returns the same resource. When the last reference goes, the resource is
not freed at once: it waits in a deferred-free queue for
CW_RES_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES frame boundaries (the GPU may still be drawing
with it), and a load of the same path in that window revives it.

Loading. cw_res_load is synchronous: it returns with the resource READY or
FAILED. cw_res_load_async reads and decodes the file in the background and
finishes it on the main thread in cw_res_frame (three.c objects, GL
uploads) under a per-frame upload budget:
  - read: natively on the job pool, together with the decode, so a
    request costs the main thread nothing but bookkeeping. In a cart the
    host's asset calls belong to the main thread (a lazily loaded web cart
    suspends there while the bytes arrive), so cw_res_frame reads at most
    a few queued files per frame (cw_res_set_read_budget). Files of the
    project layer (cartwheel/vfs.h) and of types with a prepare step (glTF)
    are read at request time, as before.
  - decode: on the job pool, at most cw_res_set_max_in_flight at once,
    started in finish order, so a late urgent request is not stuck behind
    a hundred early ones.
  - finish: in ORDER, always: by lane (lower first), then priority (higher
    first), then request order (cw_res_load_async_ex). A resource whose
    decode ended early waits for the ones before it, so the frame a
    resource becomes ready and every id three.c hands out are the same on
    every host (the order is a pure function of the requests). Plain
    cw_res_load_async is lane 0, priority 0: request order.
In a deterministic run (cw_is_deterministic_run) the budget counts bytes
only and cw_res_frame waits for the next decode instead of skipping a
frame, so readiness never depends on thread timing; otherwise a
millisecond budget applies too.

Cancelling. Releasing the last reference of a load in flight cancels it
without waiting: work not started is dropped, a decode already running
finishes on its worker and its output is discarded when it lands.

Residency. With cw_res_set_residency_budget, a resource whose last
reference goes stays loaded (READY, 0 references) in an LRU cache while
the cache fits the budget; a load of its path revives it at once (a cache
hit). The least recently released go first when the cache is over budget.

Threading: every function here is main-thread only, except the type
callbacks documented as worker-safe.

Memory: CW_MEM_RESOURCE (bookkeeping, decoded data). Payload sizes are in
cw_res_stats.

functions.name: cw_res_load
functions.doc:
Synchronous load (or a new reference to the loaded one). Never returns a
null handle for a well-formed path: check cw_res_state / cw_res_get. A
missing file FAILS with "res://x: not found (asset root: ...)" in the log.

functions.name: cw_res_load_async
functions.signature: cw_res cw_res_load_async(const char *path, cw_res_type type, cw_res_done_fn done, void *user)
functions.doc:
Asynchronous load. done may be NULL. A '#' sub-resource path loads its file
asynchronously and resolves the sub-resource when the file is ready.

functions.name: cw_res_load_async_ex
functions.signature: cw_res cw_res_load_async_ex(const char *path, cw_res_type type, const cw_res_load_opts *opts)
functions.doc:
cw_res_load_async with a lane and priority (NULL opts = lane 0, priority
0). Requesting a path already loading with a better (lane, priority)
moves it up; never down. A '#' sub-resource and the files a type's
prepare step depends on load with the same lane and priority.

functions.name: cw_res_load_uid
functions.doc: Load by UID through res.index. A UID the index does not know FAILS.

functions.name: cw_res_index_set
functions.doc:
The UID table cw_res_load_uid resolves through: res.index entries, plus
any added at run time. An editor working on a project that has no pack
(so no res.index) indexes its files with this: each file's UID from its
.cwimport sidecar, else cw_res_path_uid. Setting a path again replaces
its UID.

functions.name: cw_res_index_path
functions.doc: The indexed path of a UID (interned), NULL when unknown.

functions.name: cw_res_wait
functions.doc:
Block (running jobs meanwhile) until res is READY or FAILED. Finishes
every async load requested before it too, in order.

functions.name: cw_res_wait_all
functions.doc: finish every queued async load now, in request order (main thread)

functions.name: cw_res_group_new
functions.doc: empty group, cw_alloc'd; free with cw_res_group_free

functions.name: cw_res_group_add
functions.signature: cw_res cw_res_group_add(cw_res_group *g, const char *path, cw_res_type type)
functions.doc: Start an async load and keep it in the group.

functions.name: cw_res_preload
functions.doc:
Everything a scene needs, from the "<scene>.preload" list cwpack writes
beside every .cwscene (sub-scenes' needs first, the scene last), all
started now; without a list, just the file. Returns how many it added.

functions.name: cw_res_group_get_progress
functions.doc: O(group size); fraction is 1 for an empty group

functions.name: cw_res_group_done
functions.doc: nothing still loading

functions.name: cw_res_group_wait
functions.doc: finish the rest now, in request order

functions.name: cw_res_group_count
functions.doc: loads added (cw_res_group_add and cw_res_preload)

functions.name: cw_res_group_at
functions.doc: the group's own reference (do not release); null when i is out of range

functions.name: cw_res_group_free
functions.doc: releases every reference the group holds, then frees it; NULL is a no-op

functions.name: cw_res_release
functions.doc: null handle: no-op

functions.name: cw_res_ref_count
functions.doc: 0 for a null or stale handle

functions.name: cw_res_find
functions.doc:
── queries (no reference taken) ───────────────────────────────────
loaded / loading / pending free, else null

functions.name: cw_res_find_uid
functions.doc: by the resource's uid, loaded only (no index lookup); null when absent

functions.name: cw_res_get_state
functions.doc: CW_RES_STATE_NONE for a null or stale handle

functions.name: cw_res_is_ready
functions.doc: state is READY

functions.name: cw_res_get
functions.doc: The payload (see the type list above), NULL unless READY.

functions.name: cw_res_type_of
functions.doc: 0 for a null or stale handle

functions.name: cw_res_path
functions.doc: canonical, no "res://"; interned

functions.name: cw_res_uid
functions.doc: 0 for a null or stale handle

functions.name: cw_res_version
functions.doc:
Bumped every time the resource is (re)loaded: code that cached something
derived from it compares versions.

functions.name: cw_res_path_uid
functions.doc:
The UID a path gets without a sidecar (FNV-1a 64 of the canonical path;
identical in cwpack).

functions.name: cw_res_frame
functions.doc:
The platform calls this at the start of every frame: frees resources whose
delay ran out, finishes decoded async loads in request order under the
budget, and runs completion callbacks. Safe to call more often.

functions.name: cw_res_set_upload_budget
functions.doc:
Per-frame upload budget for async loads: stop finishing resources once
`bytes` (payload bytes: pixels uploaded, vertex data built) or `ms`
(ignored in deterministic runs) is spent. At least one resource finishes
per frame whatever its size. Defaults: 32 MB, 4 ms. 0 = unlimited.

functions.name: cw_res_set_read_budget
functions.doc:
Cart reads per frame: at most `files` queued files (at least 1 per frame
while any wait), and stop once `ms` is spent (ignored in deterministic
runs, where exactly `files` are read). Defaults: 4 files, 2 ms. Natively
reads run on the job pool and this does nothing.

functions.name: cw_res_set_max_in_flight
functions.doc:
Decodes (and native reads) running on the job pool at once; more wait
their turn, started in finish order. Default (0): half the job threads,
1 to 8, so each frame's own parallel work always finds free workers. The
jobs are background jobs (cw_job_background): the main thread never runs
a decode while it waits for other work.

functions.name: cw_res_set_residency_budget
functions.doc:
The residency cache's size: released READY resources stay loaded while
their bytes fit: payload bytes, or the file's (decompressed) bytes for
types that report none and always in a deterministic run, where they are
the same on every host. 0 (default) = no cache: the last release frees
after CW_RES_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES. Lowering it evicts at the next cw_res_frame.

functions.name: cw_res_get_stats
functions.doc: walks every slot: O(live resources)

functions.name: cw_res_get_info
functions.doc: false (out zeroed) for a null or stale handle; path is interned

functions.name: cw_res_log_report
functions.doc:
Log a load report: totals, then one line per loaded file (sizes, read /
decode / finish times, time and frames to ready). The "res" debug command
returns the same numbers as JSON.

functions.name: cw_compression_of
functions.doc: The compression a path's suffix names (".zst", ".lz4"), else NONE.

functions.name: cw_decompress
functions.signature: uint8_t *cw_decompress(cw_compression c, const void *src, size_t len, size_t *out_len)
functions.doc:
A whole buffer decompressed: a zstd frame (with or without its content
size) or an lz4 frame; NONE copies. cw_alloc'd (CW_MEM_RESOURCE) with a
NUL after the *out_len bytes; NULL for corrupt or truncated input. Any
thread. Cost: zstd decodes at roughly 1 GB/s, lz4 at several GB/s
natively (a cart runs at about half that).

functions.name: cw_decompress_block
functions.signature: bool cw_decompress_block(cw_compression c, const void *src, size_t len, void *dst, size_t raw_len)
functions.doc:
Into dst, whose size the caller knows (raw_len): a zstd frame, or a bare
lz4 BLOCK (no frame: what a cwpak entry stores). False unless exactly
raw_len bytes came out. Any thread.

functions.name: cw_res_shutdown
functions.doc:
Free everything now (the platform calls it at shutdown, before the GL
context goes). Handles all go stale.

functions.name: cw_res_prepare_dep
functions.signature: cw_res cw_res_prepare_dep(cw_res_prepare *p, const char *path, cw_res_type type)
functions.doc:
From prepare: load another resource first (its own async load; this one
finishes after it). Returns its handle (this resource holds the reference
until it is freed).

functions.name: cw_res_prepare_read
functions.doc:
From prepare: read another file now (main thread) and hand its bytes to
decode. false when it does not exist.

functions.name: cw_res_prepare_bytes
functions.doc: The file being prepared.

functions.name: cw_res_prepare_path
functions.doc: canonical, interned

functions.name: cw_res_register_type
functions.doc:
Register a type; returns its id. Registering a name twice returns the
existing id (the desc is not replaced). Main thread, before loading.

functions.name: cw_res_type_find
functions.doc: 0 when unknown

functions.name: cw_res_type_name
functions.doc: registered name; "none" when unknown

functions.name: cw_res_create
functions.signature: cw_res cw_res_create(const char *path, cw_res_type type, const void *bytes, size_t len)

functions.name: cw_res_reload_from_memory
functions.signature: bool cw_res_reload_from_memory(cw_res res, const void *bytes, size_t len)
functions.doc:
Replace a loaded resource's data with new file bytes (hot reload, or the
editor/romdev pushing a changed asset). Synchronous; the handle stays
valid, cw_res_version goes up, glTF instances are re-linked. false (and
the old data kept) if the new bytes fail to decode.

functions.name: cw_res_reload
functions.doc: Reread the file from the asset root (after cw_asset_remount) and reload.

functions.name: cw_res_register_sub
functions.signature: cw_res cw_res_register_sub(cw_res parent, const char *name, cw_res_type type, void *payload)
functions.doc:
Sub-resources: a type's finish step registers payloads it owns under
"<path>#<name>". They live as long as the parent; a reference to one keeps
the parent loaded. Returns the sub-resource handle.

functions.name: cw_res_texture
functions.doc:
owned by the resource (valid while referenced). Its colour space is the
file's, as three.js r187's loaders give it: a KTX2's DFD transfer function
(cwpack's texture.color, sRGB by default), none (data) for PNG / JPEG,
unless a glTF that shows the image (as colour or as data) claimed it before
it loaded (a glTF that finds it loaded in the other one uploads its own). It
is fixed when the resource loads (on GL the texels upload into an sRGB or a
linear format then): import a colour image as KTX2, rather than changing
color_space on the loaded texture.

functions.name: cw_res_material
functions.doc: owned by the resource (valid while referenced)

functions.name: cw_res_blob
functions.doc: for FONT / JSON / TEXT / BINARY; owned by the resource

functions.name: cw_res_audio
functions.doc: owned by the resource

functions.name: cw_res_audio_sound
functions.doc:
The clip as a cw_sound (cartwheel/audio.h), made on first call through
cw_sound_load_memory with desc (later calls return the same sound; desc is
ignored then) and freed with the resource. Needs cw_audio_init. A reload
frees it: call again after cw_res_version changes.

functions.name: cw_res_texture_info
functions.doc: false unless a READY texture

functions.name: cw_res_ktx2_target
functions.doc:
The GPU format KTX2 textures transcode to in this context (after the first
KTX2 load; "none" before).

functions.name: cw_res_mesh
functions.doc: owned by the resource (a glTF sub-resource)

functions.name: cw_res_gltf
functions.doc: owned by the resource

functions.name: cw_gltf_instantiate
functions.doc:
A new instance of the scene: a Group (yours: add it to a scene, release it
with t3_release) whose children copy the template's nodes and share its
geometry and materials. Skinned meshes get their own skeleton bound to the
instance's bones; animation clips (gltf->animations) bind by node name. An
instance holds a reference to the resource until three.c destroys it. After

headers.summary:
cartwheel/rim_light.h: a rim light, a coloured glow along a surface's
silhouette edges (a shading part, cartwheel/shading.h).

Where a surface turns away from the camera its edge glows in the rim's
colour: glow = color x strength x (1 - N.V)^power, added to the
material's emissive light (so it shows in shadow and at night, and bloom
picks it up). It fades in with distance from the camera: below
`near` metres it is `close` of its full strength, past `far` it is all
of it, smooth in between. That is what a split-screen shooter wants for
telling teams apart: a fighter 30 m away reads as a red or blue outline,
one at arm's length is not painted over. Also: a highlight on pickups or
interactive objects, a "spawn protected" shimmer (pulse the strength from
code), a selection glow in a menu scene.

Per material: every mesh drawing the material gets the same rim (glTF
instances share their file's materials: clone a material per character,
t3_material_clone, for a per-character colour; MeshInstance3D primitives
of one look share one material in a tree). Changing the values is free (a
uniform per draw); the part is added once.

Works on MeshStandardMaterial and MeshPhysicalMaterial, skinned or not,
with every other part (clustered lights, the cascaded sun, skin shading,
GI). Costs a few ALU operations per pixel of the material; nothing when
no material has a rim. Shadow casters are untouched. Every quality preset
draws it (it is a readability feature, not decoration).

Program tables: a material with a rim draws the composed state with
"rim" in its extension (xrim, xcluster_rim_gi, ...): tools/programs.mjs
finds and adds those like any other state.

headers.summary:
cartwheel scene model: nodes, the scene tree, groups, signals, reflection.

A node is a named element of a tree. Its TYPE (registered once) says what
data it carries, which properties it exposes by name (reflection), which
signals it can emit and which lifecycle callbacks it has. Node types
inherit: Node3D extends Node, MeshInstance3D extends Node3D. Users hold
nodes by generational handle (cw_node); a freed node's handle reads as
null, never as another node.

Processing order is tree order (depth first, children in order), so a run
is deterministic. Adding or removing nodes while the tree is being
processed is queued and applied at the end of the current phase.

Every property is reachable by name (cw_node_set / cw_node_get) with typed
values (cw_value). That one path serves the editor's inspector, the text
scene format, animation tracks, romdev's debug channel and script bindings.

headers.summary:
2D for the scene tree: the canvas node types over the batched 2D renderer
(render2d.h), and the tree's 2D pass.

── node types (all properties reflected: .cwscene, inspector, debug channel) ──
Every type below except CanvasLayer and CanvasSettings extends Node2D
(position, rotation, scale, skew, z_index, z_relative, visible,
interpolate, modulate, self_modulate). Pixels, y down, radians clockwise.
Point lists ("points", "polygon") are strings of numbers taken in pairs:
"0 0, 32 0, 32 16". Textures and fonts are asset paths, loaded (and cached
by path) on first draw, so scenes instance without a GL context.

  Sprite2D          texture, filter (LINEAR|NEAREST), centered, offset,
                    flip_h, flip_v, region_enabled, region (vec4 x y w h),
                    hframes, vframes, frame (atlas grid cell)
  AnimatedSprite2D  texture, filter, hframes, vframes (the atlas grid),
                    regions ("x y w h, x y w h ..." : an explicit frame list
                    that replaces the grid when set), animations
                    ("idle@4:0-1; run@10:2-5; jump:6!" : name, optional fps,
                    frames as indices and ranges, '!' = play once),
                    animation (current name; empty = the first), fps
                    (default for animations without @fps), speed_scale,
                    playing, frame, process (FIXED: advances on fixed ticks
                    by the fixed dt, deterministic for replays; FRAME: by
                    the frame dt), centered, offset, flip_h, flip_v.
                    Signals: frame_changed, animation_finished.
  NinePatch2D       texture, filter, region, size, patch_left/top/right/bottom,
                    margin_scale, draw_center, centered
  Line2D            points, width, color, closed
  Polygon2D         polygon, color, texture (optional; uv = point / texture size), offset
  Label2D           text, font, font_mode (SDF|BITMAP), bake_size, size, color,
                    align (LEFT|CENTER|RIGHT), wrap_width, line_spacing, letter_spacing
                    (the text box's top-left sits at the node's origin)
  TileMap2D         tileset (texture), filter, tile_size, margin, spacing,
                    columns, cell_size, layers (1..8), cells0..cells7,
                    animations ("4:2@6; 10:4@8" : tile id, frame count, fps).
                    Cells text form: rows separated by '/', cells by spaces;
                    '.' = empty, N = tile id (0-based index into the tileset
                    grid), suffix x / y / d = flip x / flip y / transpose,
                    "N*k" (or ".*k") repeats a cell k times:
                    "0*20 / . . 3 3x / 1*4". The map's size is the largest
                    row count and row length over all layers.
  Camera2D          current, zoom, offset, anchor_top_left, smoothing,
                    smoothing_speed, limit_left/top/right/bottom, rotating.
                    The first current Camera2D in tree order drives every
                    canvas that follows the viewport (the default canvas,
                    ParallaxLayers, CanvasLayers with follow_viewport).
                    Smoothing runs on fixed ticks (cw_camera2d_follow,
                    deterministic) after physics; rendering interpolates.
  CanvasLayer       (a Node) layer (draw order; the default canvas is 0),
                    offset, rotation, scale, follow_viewport, visible, y_sort.
                    Defaults (as in Godot): layer 1 (above the default
                    canvas), follow_viewport false (screen space: a HUD;
                    set it for a layer that scrolls with the Camera2D),
                    offset 0, rotation 0, scale 1, visible, no y_sort.
                    Its descendants' transforms start fresh at the layer.
  ParallaxLayer     motion_scale (camera factor), motion_offset; its
                    descendants draw in their own render layer just above
                    the canvas they are in (put them under a CanvasLayer
                    with a negative layer for a background).
  Light2D           enabled, color, energy, range (radius px), falloff,
                    height, shadow. A canvas holding a light is drawn lit.
  LightOccluder2D   polygon, closed (casts shadows for lights with shadow)
  CanvasSettings    (a Node; the first one in tree order counts)
                    virtual_width/virtual_height (0 = window pixels),
                    scale_mode (NONE|INTEGER|FIT|STRETCH|EXPAND), clear_color,
                    letterbox, ambient (light where no Light2D reaches on
                    lit canvases), pixel_snap, y_sort (default canvas).
                    Defaults: no virtual canvas, scale_mode NONE, clear
                    and letterbox opaque black, ambient white (lit canvases
                    fully lit), no pixel_snap, no y_sort. A tree with no
                    CanvasSettings draws the same way: window pixels,
                    cleared to black, ambient white.

── two coordinate spaces: Node2D vs Control ─────────────────────────────
Node2Ds (everything above) live on the VIRTUAL canvas when CanvasSettings
sets one: positions, sizes and camera are virtual pixels, scaled to the
window by scale_mode. Controls (cartwheel/ui.h: Label, Button, ...) do
not: the scene runner draws the UI in its own window pass, so their
anchors and offsets are UI units, window pixels divided by cw_ui_scale,
even under a CanvasLayer and even with a virtual canvas. With a 320x180
virtual canvas in a 640x360 window, a Label at offset_left 8 sits 8
window pixels (4 virtual pixels) from the edge. This is deliberate: UI
text stays sharp and keeps its size whatever the game's resolution. To
lay UI out in virtual pixels instead, set cw_ui_set_scale(window height /
virtual height), or draw the UI inside your own virtual pass with
cw_ui_draw (pixel-art UI that scales with the game; see ui.h).

── the 2D pass ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cw_canvas_draw walks the tree once in tree order: hidden Node2Ds and
CanvasLayers hide their subtrees, transforms compose (interpolated between
the last two fixed ticks for nodes with `interpolate`), modulate
multiplies down, z_index adds down while z_relative. Every canvas item is
submitted to render2d in its canvas's render layer at its z, so the
renderer's stable sort draws by (canvas layer, z, tree order) and y within
y-sorted canvases. Canvases get render layers 0.. in (layer, tree order)
order; a frame may hold up to 30.

Who draws on top (the UI hook): after the tree's 2D pass ends,
cw_canvas_draw runs the tree's registered overlay passes
(cw_canvas_add_pass) in `order`. Each runs its OWN render2d pass
(cw_r2d_begin with clear = false ... cw_r2d_end) over the frame, so UI
(Control nodes) composites over 3D and 2D without sharing layer slots.

The scene runner draws: 3D (only when a Camera3D exists; a 2D-only tree
never creates a three.c renderer), then cw_canvas_draw. When nothing in
the tree is a canvas item and no overlay pass is registered, the 2D pass
is skipped entirely.

headers.summary:
Scene files (.cwscene): a node subtree as text that diffs and merges in git.

  [scene format=1]
  [ext_scene id=1 path="player/player.cwscene"]

  [node name="Level" type="Node3D"]
  position = vec3(0, 0, 0)

  [node name="Player" parent="." instance=1 groups="players"]
  position = vec3(0, 1.5, 4)

  [node name="Sun" parent="." type="DirectionalLight3D"]
  energy = 3

  [node name="Mesh" parent="Player"]      <- no type, no instance: an OVERRIDE
  color = color(1, 0, 0, 1)               of the instanced scene's node

  [connection signal="body_entered" from="Goal" to="." method="on_goal"]

Rules: one property per line (`name = value`, values as cw_value_format
writes them); parent paths are relative to the scene root ("." = root);
only properties that differ from the type's defaults (or, inside an
instance, from the instanced scene) are written; nodes in tree order.
Node-valued properties are node("path") from the scene root ("." = the
root), resolved after the whole instance is built.
Lines starting with `;` or `#` are comments: the loader skips them and
cw_scene_save does not keep them (it writes the tree, not the old text),
so an editor save drops them. Saving the result of a load reproduces a
file in that canonical form byte for byte. Docs listings select scene
sections by node (docs/AUTHORING.md), never by comment markers.

functions.name: cw_scene_parse
functions.doc:
Parse scene text. path names the file for errors and resolves ext_scene
paths (relative to the asset root). NULL on a parse error (logged with
the line number). Packed scenes are cached by path.

functions.name: cw_scene_load
functions.doc:
Load + parse a scene (cached by path). Reads through the project layer
(cartwheel/vfs.h: written-but-unexported files and a native project
directory first), then the app's assets.

functions.name: cw_scene_cache_forget
functions.doc:
Drop a path from the load cache (NULL = every path), so the next load
reads the file again: call it after rewriting a scene (an editor saving a
sub-scene). Packed scenes already loaded stay valid for the nodes made
from them.

functions.name: cw_scene_instance
functions.doc: Build a new node subtree from a packed scene (not in a tree yet).

functions.name: cw_scene_instance_path
functions.doc: cw_scene_load + cw_scene_instance; null handle (logged) when the scene is missing

functions.name: cw_scene_instance_linked
functions.doc:
Instance a scene AS AN INSTANCE: the new root remembers its source, so
saving the tree it is added to writes `instance=` plus only the
properties that differ (what an editor's "instance a scene" does);
cw_scene_instance_path makes a plain copy whose nodes save in full.

functions.name: cw_scene_instance_source
functions.doc:
The scene path n was instanced from (n is the root of a linked or
scene-file instance), else NULL.

functions.name: cw_packed_scene_free
functions.doc:
Free a packed scene from cw_scene_parse once nothing will instance it
again (nodes already made from it do not need it). Cached scenes
(cw_scene_load) are refused.

functions.name: cw_scene_save
functions.doc: Write a subtree as scene text; returns a cw_alloc'd string.

functions.name: cw_packed_scene_path
functions.doc: interned asset path, "(memory)" for unnamed text; ps must not be NULL

functions.name: cw_scene_register_section
functions.doc: The descriptor must outlive the program (static). Idempotent per name.

functions.name: cw_scene_attr
functions.doc: `key=value` or `key="value"` of a section header (interned; NULL when absent)

functions.name: cw_scene_node_in_instance
functions.doc:
true when n (or an ancestor below root) is the root of an instanced
sub-scene: its data belongs to that scene's file

functions.name: cw_scene_app
functions.doc:
── the scene runner ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
An app that runs a tree: instance `main_scene` under the root, fixed
ticks / updates / pre_render through the tree, then draw its 3D scene
(and later 2D layers and UI). `base` may supply title/size/debug/workers
and extra callbacks (called after the tree's own): base.render runs after
the 3D draw, so a HUD drawn there with render2d lands on top (the runner
resets three.c's GL state cache afterwards). main_scene may be NULL: build
the tree in base.init through cw_scene_app_tree(). Physics worlds made with
physics3d.h directly are stepped by the app, in base.fixed_update.

functions.name: cw_scene_app_tree
functions.doc: the runner's tree; NULL before the app starts

functions.name: cw_scene_app_change_scene
functions.doc:
Replace the main scene (or, with none, everything under the root) with a
new instance of path. The project layer's copy (cartwheel/vfs.h) wins over
the asset; reread parses the text again instead of using the cache (the
debug channel's reload_scene). false (logged) when it does not load.

functions.name: cw_scene_app_current_scene
functions.doc: NULL when the app has none

types.name: cw_packed_scene
types.decl: typedef struct cw_packed_scene cw_packed_scene;

types.name: cw_scene_section
types.doc:
── extending the format ─────────────────────────────────────────────
Modules store data that is not node properties (animations, ...) in
sections of their own. A section starts at its `[name ...]` header and
owns every following line, and the sub-headers it declares (`[track ...]`),
until the next section header. Extension sections are written after the
nodes and before the connections, extensions in registration order.

headers.summary:
cartwheel/shading.h: shading parts, three.c generator extensions that
stack on one material.

three.c gives a material one generator extension (t3_material_set_extension,
state x<name>): r187 TSL captured into a program, filled at run time by a C
hook. Several engine features change how every surface shades (terrain or
water decide the surface, clustered lights add direct light, the GI module
adds reflections and bounce light), so one material often needs more than
one. A part is one such extension; a material carries a list of parts, and
its extension is the composed name: the parts in the fixed order below,
joined by '_' ("terrain_gi", "cluster_gi"). Nothing is written by hand per
combination:

  - the generator side: a part is a module src/<module>/extensions/<part>.mjs
    (export name, apply()), as any extension. tools/programs.mjs writes, for
    every composed state a manifest names (standard+senv+xcluster_gi), a
    module that applies the parts in that order to the capture's material,
    and hands it to three.c's generator. Surface parts set colorNode,
    normalNode, positionNode; lighting parts add an r187 LightingNode to the
    material's lights; the GI part sets envNode (reflections) and adds a
    LightingNode (the probe grid's irradiance). So parts compose without
    knowing each other, as long as each names its uniforms and textures
    "ext.<unique name>" and its shared uniform groups uniquely.
  - the run-time side: each part registers its fill hook on a renderer
    (cw_shading_part); a composed extension's hook calls every part's hook
    in order on the same draw.

Order (fixed, global): surface parts (terrain, terrainlow, terrainfar,
water), then lighting (cluster), then indirect light (gi); any other part
between lighting and indirect, by name.

Cost: none per part beyond its own hook. three.c does not auto-instance a
mesh whose material carries an extension (each such mesh is its own draw)
unless every part of it says its hook reads nothing of the object
(cw_shading_part_batching): then meshes sharing geometry and material are
one instanced draw, as plain ones are.

functions.name: cw_shading_part
functions.signature: void cw_shading_part(t3_renderer *r, const char *name, t3_extension_fill fill, void *user)
functions.doc:
The renderer's hook for part `name` ([a-z0-9], up to 15 characters): it
fills that part's "ext." values for each draw of any material carrying the
part, alone or composed. fill NULL removes it. Also installs every composed
extension that includes the part.

functions.name: cw_shading_part_batching
functions.signature: void cw_shading_part_batching(t3_renderer *r, const char *name, bool on)
functions.doc:
Part `name`'s hook on r reads nothing of the object it fills for (only
per-frame values, or ones a batch keeps equal: receive_shadow, render
order), so meshes whose material carries it may be auto-instanced. A
composed extension batches when all of its parts do. Off by default.

functions.name: cw_shading_part_known
functions.doc:
A part named `name` was registered (cw_shading_part) on some renderer: the
engine's lighting composes its own parts (cluster, csm) with it.

functions.name: cw_shading_forget
functions.doc: Forget a renderer (before t3_renderer_destroy).

functions.name: cw_shading_add
functions.doc:
Add part `name` to material m (no-op when it has it): m's extension becomes
the composed name. false when m would carry more than CW_SHADING_MAX_PARTS
parts or the composed name would pass 31 characters.

functions.name: cw_shading_remove
functions.doc: Remove part `name` from m (no-op when it lacks it).

functions.name: cw_shading_has
functions.doc: m carries part `name`.

functions.name: cw_shading_set
functions.signature: bool cw_shading_set(t3_material *m, const char *const *parts, int n)
functions.doc:
Replace m's parts by the composed name of `parts` (n of them, any order):
what cw_shading_add gives, from scratch.

headers.summary:
cartwheel/shell.h: the plumbing around a game's play, so a game writes only
its gameplay and art.

  loading screen -> title (Play, Settings, Quit) -> join (1-4 players) ->
  play <-> pause (Resume, Settings, Quit to title)

Settings: graphics (cartwheel/quality.h; left / right step the preset,
accept opens the graphics page of cartwheel/quality_menu.h with every
setting), music and effects volume, screen shake (Full, Reduced, Off: games
scale their camera shake by cw_shell_screen_shake) and the controls (each
action's bindings). They are saved, with the game's own save data, in one
versioned, checksummed block the shell keeps in cw_app_desc.save.

  static cw_app_desc desc = { ... };
  desc.save = cw_shell_save_region();          // in cw_main
  desc.save_size = cw_shell_save_region_size();

  static void init(void) {
    cw_shell_init(&(cw_shell_desc){ .title = "My Game", .max_players = 4,
                                    .game_save_size = sizeof(my_save), .start = start_match });
    my_save *s = cw_shell_game_save();         // zeroed when there was none
  }
  static void fixed_update(double dt) {
    if (!cw_shell_update()) return;            // menus own this tick
    ... gameplay for cw_shell_players() players ...
  }
  static void render(double alpha) {
    ... the game's frame ...
    cw_shell_draw();                           // menus and overlays on top
  }

Input: menus read the actions ui_up, ui_down, ui_left, ui_right,
ui_accept, ui_back and pause, which the shell defines (keyboard arrows and
WASD, Enter / Space, Escape; pad d-pad and left stick, South, East,
Start), and pointer taps (mouse or touch) on menu items. On the join
screen each pad joins with South and leaves with East, the keyboard joins
with Enter; players are assigned their pad and devices (cw_input_assign)
in join order, so gameplay asks cw_action_* for players 0..n-1.

Split screen: cw_shell_split lays one view per player out with the
pipeline (cw_pipeline_split: two side by side, three and four in quadrants,
three leaving the fourth quadrant for a shared HUD); cw_shell_player_rect
and cw_shell_shared_rect give the HUD where to draw.

Audio: the shell starts the mixer (cw_audio_init) unless the game did,
and then runs its per-frame update from cw_shell_draw. Two buses under the master, "music" and "sfx", follow the volume
settings; play the game's music and effects on them. The sound hook plays
the menus' sounds (move, select, back, join, pause), the screen hook starts
each screen's music.

A scene app's tree (cw_scene_app) is paused outside play, so its nodes
hold still under the menus.

Determinism: menus run in fixed_update from the input snapshot, so a
replay drives them like gameplay. A test or an autopilot build skips them
with cw_shell_start. Debug fields: shell.screen, shell.players, shell.item.

functions.name: cw_shell_save_region
functions.doc:
The save region for cw_app_desc.save / save_size: the shell's settings and
the game's save data. Static, so cw_main can name it before init.

functions.name: cw_shell_save_region_size
functions.doc: its size in bytes

functions.name: cw_shell_init
functions.doc:

the saved settings, defines the ui actions and the audio buses.

The game's save data: game_save_size bytes, zeroed when the save was
missing or from another version. Write it, then cw_shell_save_commit.

functions.name: cw_shell_update

functions.doc:
Start a match now with n players (pads 0..n-1, player 0 also on the
keyboard, mouse and touch): an autopilot build or a test skips the menus.

functions.name: cw_shell_join_open
functions.doc:
Join and leave during play: opens the join screen over the running match (play pauses, exactly as for the pause
menu) with the current players on their seats. A pad presses A to take a free seat, B to leave its own seat;
Start or Enter confirms (at least one player stays) and play resumes with players_changed; B on a pad that
has no seat cancels and leaves everything as it was. Seats keep their numbers: a leaver's seat reads no
input (cw_shell_seat_taken says which are held), a newcomer takes the first free seat, and the match's
player count is the highest seat held plus one. Returns false (and does nothing) outside play or in a one
player game.

functions.name: cw_shell_seat_taken
functions.doc:
Is this player seat held by a pad or the keyboard (0 .. cw_shell_players() - 1)? Right after a start every
seat below the player count is; after cw_shell_join_open a seat can be empty.

functions.name: cw_shell_join_requested
functions.doc:
True on the tick a pad or the keyboard that has no seat presses A (Enter) or Start: the cue for a game to
offer cw_shell_join_open, say between rounds. Poll it in fixed_update after cw_shell_update.

functions.name: cw_shell_join_press
functions.doc:
One-press join during play: if a pad that has no seat pressed A this tick, it takes
the first free seat at once, with no join screen, players_changed tells the game, and this returns true (the
seat number, like every seat, never changes while the match runs). False outside play, in a one player game,
when no seat is free, or when nobody without a seat pressed A. Call it in fixed_update after cw_shell_update;
cw_shell_join_open stays the way to leave a seat or rearrange. Pads only: the keyboard already drives a player.

functions.doc: end the match and show the title (every pad drives the menus again)

The factor a game multiplies every camera shake, kick and bob by: 1 for Full, CW_SHELL_SHAKE_REDUCED_SCALE for

headers.summary:
cartwheel/skin_shading.h: skin shading, a cheap subsurface look for
characters (a shading part, cartwheel/shading.h).

Real skin scatters light under its surface: the shadow side of a face goes
soft and warm instead of dark grey, and thin parts (ears, nostrils, finger
webs) glow when lit from behind. Plain PBR shades skin like painted
plastic. This part adds two cheap terms to the material's own lighting
(MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhysicalMaterial, so sheen, clear coat and
the rest still apply), for every light that reaches it (the scene's own
lights, clustered lights, the cascaded sun):

  - wrap: diffuse light reaches past the line where the surface turns away
    from the light, each colour channel by `wrap` times its `scatter`
    component, so red bleeds furthest (a warm, soft terminator). The lit
    side is unchanged; the extra light is (N.L + w) / (1 + w) - N.L.
  - translucency: light from behind the surface, seen through it: strongest
    looking toward a light past a thin edge. r187's MeshSSSNodeMaterial
    term (fast translucency): pow(saturate(V . -(L + N * distortion)),
    power) + ambient, times `translucency`, the scatter colour, the
    surface's diffuse colour and the light's colour.

No screen-space pass, no extra render targets, no textures: a few ALU
operations per light per skin pixel. A light's shadow darkens both terms
as it darkens the rest of the light, so translucency needs the light not
to be blocked by the body itself (a rim light behind a head, say).

Quality: on Low (cw_quality_scale("skin") is 0) every skin material draws
as its plain PBR material (the part is removed, so Low pays nothing); the
other presets draw it. The engine switches when the setting changes.

From glTF: a material loaded through the resource system (CW_RES_GLTF)
gets skin shading when the file asks for it:
  - KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission: translucency = its
    diffuseTransmissionFactor, scatter = its diffuseTransmissionColorFactor
    (the rest as cw_skin_shading_default);
  - extras "skin_shading": true (the defaults) or an object with any of
    "scatter" [r, g, b], "wrap", "translucency", "distortion", "power",
    "ambient" (over the defaults, or over what the extension gave).
Or by material name after loading: cw_skin_shading_apply_named.

Cost: see docs/guides/rendering-3d.md, "Characters".

functions.name: cw_skin_shading_default
functions.doc:
the defaults above (a light-skinned human; darker skin wants a deeper
scatter, e.g. 0.9, 0.3, 0.2, and less translucency)

functions.name: cw_skin_shading_apply
functions.doc:
Shade material m as skin (d NULL: the defaults). m must be a
MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhysicalMaterial; false otherwise, or when m
already carries CW_SHADING_MAX_PARTS parts. Applying again replaces the
values. The material is retained until cw_skin_shading_remove. Every mesh
drawing m is affected (glTF instances share their file's materials: clone
a material for a per-character tint).

functions.name: cw_skin_shading_remove
functions.doc: Back to plain PBR (no-op when m is not skin).

functions.name: cw_skin_shading_get
functions.doc: m is skin; its values into *out when out is not NULL.

functions.doc:
Every material named `material_name` (t3_material.name: the glTF
material's name) on the meshes under root gets skin shading. Returns how
many materials (each counted once).

functions.doc: Materials shaded as skin now.

functions.name: cw_skin_shading_enabled
functions.doc:
The quality setting draws skin shading (false on Low: skin materials draw
