headers.summary:
cartwheel/splats.h: blob shadows and light splats, the cheap stand-ins
for dynamic shadows and dynamic lights on ground that draws baked
(LightmapGI shading BAKED, cartwheel/lightmap.h, takes no real-time light
or shadow).

A splat set is one instanced draw of flat quads lying on the ground, each
placed, stretched and turned by the caller every frame:

  CW_SPLATS_SHADOW  a soft dark blob under a moving object: the colour
                    below is multiplied by 1 - strength x falloff (blend
                    ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR), so a strength of 0.6
                    takes 60% of the light at the centre. Stretch it away
                    from the sun for a low sun's long shadow.
  CW_SPLATS_LIGHT   a pool of added light on the ground under a moving
                    light (a muzzle flash, a fire, a lamp a player
                    carries): additive, the colour is the light's colour
                    x strength (HDR, so it blooms), the falloff that of a
                    point light above the ground.

Cost: one draw for the whole set; pixels only where a splat lies (a
shadow under 2000 enemies is a few percent of a 1080p frame). Splats test
depth and write none, so what stands on them hides them. Render only:
nothing here reaches the simulation. Opt in: nothing draws a splat unless
a game makes a set.

functions.name: cw_splats_new
functions.signature: cw_splats *cw_splats_new(cw_node parent, const char *name, cw_splats_kind kind, int capacity)
functions.doc:
A set of up to `capacity` splats drawn under a new Node3D `name`, a
child of parent. NULL when capacity < 1.

functions.name: cw_splats_free
functions.doc: removes its node too; NULL is a no-op

functions.name: cw_splats_begin
functions.doc: Start this frame's splats (none drawn until added).

functions.name: cw_splats_add
functions.signature: bool cw_splats_add(cw_splats *s, t3_vec3 at, float length, float width, float yaw, float offset, t3_color color, float strength)
functions.doc:
One splat centred at `at` (its height: the ground's, a few centimetres are
added against z-fighting), `length` along its yaw (radians about +Y, 0 =
along +Z) and `width` across, metres. strength: SHADOW 0..1 (the share of
the light taken at its centre); LIGHT any (x color). The centre can sit
off the middle: `offset` (-1..1) slides it toward the far end, for a long
shadow that starts at the caster's feet. false when the set is full.

functions.name: cw_splats_add_lights
functions.signature: int cw_splats_add_lights(cw_splats *s, cw_node root, float ground_y, float scale)
functions.doc:
A LIGHT set: a splat under every visible OmniLight3D under root that has
energy and is not baked (bake_direct off), sized to where its light on
ground at height ground_y falls to a twentieth (at most its range), its
strength the light's irradiance straight below (energy / height^2) x
scale: give scale the ground's albedo / PI and the pool is about the
light a lit ground would show. Returns how many it added.

functions.name: cw_splats_set_texture
functions.doc:
Replace the set's falloff with a texture of your own (retained; its rgb
is the strength across the splat, centred, fading to black at the edge):
a wet sheen that shows the asphalt's damp patches, a lamp's gobo. NULL
puts the built-in falloff back.

functions.name: cw_splats_end
functions.doc: Upload this frame's splats (after the last add).

functions.name: cw_splats_count
functions.doc: splats added since cw_splats_begin

functions.name: cw_splats_mesh
functions.doc: The set's instanced mesh (render order, layers, visibility).

types.name: cw_splats_kind
types.decl: typedef enum { CW_SPLATS_SHADOW, CW_SPLATS_LIGHT } cw_splats_kind;

types.name: cw_splats
types.decl: typedef struct cw_splats cw_splats;

headers.summary:
cartwheel world streaming: a big world cut into square cells that load,
activate, deactivate and unload around the player while the game runs,
with no loading screen.

── cells ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The world is a cells_x x cells_z grid of cell_size metre squares on the XZ
plane, cell (0, 0)'s min corner at `origin`. Cell (cx, cz) has id
cz * cells_x + cx and, when path_format is set, one file of its own
(snprintf(path, path_format, cx, cz)): one file per cell, so a lazily
loaded web cart waits on one cell at most. A ".zst" / ".lz4" suffix
decompresses on the job pool (cartwheel/resource.h). Every cell needs its
file; an empty cell is a small file.

A cell moves through:
  NONE      not wanted
  LOADING   its file is loading (cw_res_load_async_ex, nearest first)
  LOADED    on_load ran (on the main thread, from cw_stream_frame, at
            most prepare_per_frame cells a frame): what is only drawn
            (meshes, terrain, scatter) exists and shows
  ACTIVE    on_activate ran (from cw_stream_tick): what the simulation
            sees (bodies, navmesh tiles, entities) exists
and back down: on_deactivate (tick) then on_unload (tick), after which
the file is released (cw_res_set_residency_budget can keep it cached).

── sources and radii ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Sources (the player, the camera, a remote player) say where cells are
needed. A cell is wanted LOADED while its square comes within
load_radius of a source (horizontal distance, the nearest point of the
square), and ACTIVE within active_radius (<= load_radius). Hysteresis: a
cell leaves a set only once it is farther than radius + hysteresis, so a
player on a border does not make cells thrash. Loads start nearest first
(source priority, then distance, then id), at most max_requests_per_tick
a tick.

── determinism ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
What the simulation sees changes only in cw_stream_tick (call it from
fixed_update), and only from the sources' positions: cells activate and
deactivate in cell id order on the tick their distance says, whatever the
disk, the network or the job pool did. When a cell must activate and its
file has not arrived (or on_load has not run), the tick waits for it: a
STALL, counted in the stats (stalls, stall_ms). That keeps every host
identical; size load_radius from your IO so stalls never happen
(load_radius - active_radius is the distance the source travels while a
cell loads). activation_hash folds every (tick, cell, on/off) event: equal
hashes mean equal activation histories.

── large worlds: the floating origin ──────────────────────────────────
Positions far from the origin lose float precision (at 8 km a float
steps 1 mm; at 100 km, 8 mm, and the camera shakes). The stream keeps a
LOCAL origin in double precision: everything the game simulates and draws
lives in local float coordinates near it, and world positions are
cw_dvec3. When the first source gets farther than rebase_distance from
the local origin (horizontally), cw_stream_tick moves the origin by whole
cells toward it (shift = a whole number of cells, so a power-of-two
cell_size keeps every shifted coordinate exact where precision allows),
then calls on_rebase with the shift: move your bodies
(cw_world3d_shift_origin) and objects by -shift. Cells get on_cell_rebase
with their new local origin. It happens on a tick the sources decide, so
it is deterministic. Rendering is camera-relative as a result: the camera
and everything near it are near the local origin.

Threads: main thread only. Callbacks run on the main thread.
Memory: CW_MEM_GAME for the grid (cells_x * cells_z small records).

headers.summary:
cartwheel terrain: heightmap terrain drawn with CDLOD, collided through
Box3D's height field, painted with Terrain3D's control-map layout, and
covered with deterministic scatter (grass, rocks, trees).

── data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A terrain is a grid of (size_x + 1) x (size_z + 1) height samples,
vertex_spacing metres apart, its sample (0, 0) at `origin`. Heights are
uint16 steps between min_height and max_height:
  y = origin.y + min_height + q * (max_height - min_height) / 65535
which is exactly how Box3D's height field stores them, so physics,
gameplay (cw_terrain_height_at) and the drawn surface agree. Each sample
also carries a control word in Terrain3D's layout (bits 31..27 base layer,
26..22 overlay layer, 21..14 blend, 13..10 uv rotation in 1/16 turns,
9..7 uv scale step, bit 2 hole; cw_terrain_control below), so painted maps
from Terrain3D's tools mean the same thing here.

Triangles: every quad splits along the diagonal from its (x, z + 1)
corner to its (x + 1, z) corner, as Box3D's height field does.

── drawing (CDLOD) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The terrain is a quadtree of patches. Each frame a camera selects the
patches to draw (cw_terrain_update): a patch of level L covers
grid_quads << L quads and is drawn with the same grid_quads x grid_quads
grid, so its vertices are 2^L samples apart. Level L is used within
lod0_range * lod_ratio^L metres of the camera (3D distance, so mountains
get the detail they need) and its odd vertices morph vertically into the
next level's triangles before that range ends, so neighbouring levels meet
without cracks or skirts. Selection runs on the job pool (one job per
root patch, results in root order), culls patches against the view
frustum four children at a time with SIMD, and sorts what it keeps front
to back. Every selected patch is one instance of one InstancedMesh: the
whole near terrain is one draw, the far terrain another.

Shading is three.js r187's MeshStandardMaterial (lights, shadows, fog and
environment are three.js's own) with a TSL extension of cartwheel's
(src/terrain/extensions): the height fetch and morph in the vertex stage;
in the fragment stage the splat of 8 layers by the control map (the two
strongest at a point, weighted from the four control texels round it),
triplanar on steep slopes, and past far_distance only a baked macro colour
and the normal map (two texture reads). Patches wholly past far_distance
draw with a third program that reads only those two.

Quality (cartwheel/quality.h, effects detail):
  Low     nearest control texel (base + overlay: 2 layers), no triplanar,
          far distance x0.5        (the Vega 8 class default)
  Medium  nearest control texel, triplanar on steep slopes, far x0.75
  High    Medium's shading (two layers weighted from 4 control texels,
          height blending, triplanar), far x1
  Ultra   High, far x1.5 and patch ranges x1.25
and the scatter's density follows cw_quality_scale("grass") / ("scatter").

Shadows: the terrain receives shadows and (cast_shadow) casts them: the
shadow pass draws the near patches with the same extension's caster
program (depth+instbig+xterrain), morphed for the viewing camera, so the
shadow follows the drawn surface. Patches past far_distance never cast.

── physics ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cw_terrain_attach_physics makes one static body with one Box3D height
field per region (region_size quads square, regions share their edge
samples and one global height range, so they line up exactly). Holes
(control bit 2) are holes for physics too. cw_shape3d_heightfield and
cw_heightfield3d (physics3d.h) are the same height field on its own.

── scatter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Scatter layers place copies of a mesh over the terrain in square cells:
32 m, doubled while that stays within a quarter of the layer's visible
range (trees at 600 m use 128 m cells: a few dozen draws, not hundreds).
Placement is a pure function of (cell, layer seed) by integer hashing:
the same instances on every host, at any worker count, whatever the
camera did. A candidate is kept by the layer's density (per square
metre), its density map, the control layers it may stand on and the
slope. Each cell is one InstancedMesh per mesh LOD with its own bounding
sphere; cells are generated on the job pool when the camera comes within
range, frustum culled, and posed each frame on the job pool: instances
shrink to nothing over the last `fade` metres of visible_range (no pop),
and switch mesh LOD by distance.

── threads ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Main thread, outside physics steps, like the rest of the scene. The
functions spread their own work over cw_jobs.

── node types (properties: docs/nodes.json) ───────────────────────────
  Terrain3D         (Node3D) a terrain: heightmap (16-bit PNG or .r16),
                    control (a Terrain3D control map as a PNG: RGBA = the
                    word's bytes, big end in R) or splat (an RGBA weight
                    image for layers 0..3), layer0_albedo .. layer7_*,
                    sizes, heights, LOD settings, physics. Placing the
                    node moves the terrain (translation only).
  TerrainScatter3D  (Node) a scatter layer of its parent Terrain3D: mesh
                    (a primitive or a glTF resource), density, density_map,
                    layers (bit mask of the control layers it grows on),
                    slope, scale range, visible_range, fade, LOD meshes,
                    cast_shadow, seed.

types.name: cw_terrain_def
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_terrain_def {
  int size_x, size_z;       /* quads; multiples of grid_quads: 512 x 512 */
  int region_size;          /* quads per physics region (power of two): 256 */
  float vertex_spacing;     /* metres between samples: 1 */
  float min_height, max_height; /* metres: 0, 100 */
  t3_vec3 origin;           /* world position of sample (0, 0) at height 0 */
  int grid_quads;           /* quads along a patch's side (power of two, 8..64): 32 */
  int lod_count;            /* levels (0 = as many as the sizes allow, at most CW_TERRAIN_MAX_LODS) */
  float lod0_range;         /* metres level 0 reaches; 0 = 2.5 patch widths (raised to that if smaller) */
  float lod_ratio;          /* each level reaches this much farther: 2 */
  float morph_start;        /* where morphing starts inside a level's band, 0..1: 0.66 */
  float far_distance;       /* metres: past it only the macro colour is drawn (0 = 400) */
  float far_fade;           /* metres over which splat fades into macro: 0 = far_distance / 4 */
  float visible_range;      /* patches farther than this are not drawn: 0 = unlimited */
  bool no_shadow_cast;      /* the near patches cast shadows unless this is set: false */
} cw_terrain_def;

types.name: cw_terrain_set
types.doc:
── terrain sets: terrain that streams with a world's cells ────────────
A big world (cartwheel/stream.h) is too big for one height grid: a 16 km
square at 2 m would be 67 M samples. A terrain set holds one small
terrain per loaded cell instead, all with the same definition, sharing
one template terrain's layer textures (cw_terrain_share_layers) and
getting the same scatter layers (each cell its own seed). Neighbouring
cells must repeat their shared edge samples; with equal definitions their
LOD bands line up, so cells meet without cracks. The set draws every
terrain from one SHADOW-phase pipeline pass ("terrainset") of its tree.
Physics: each cell's height fields are built when it is added, and its
static bodies are created only while it is active. Main thread.
types.decl: typedef struct cw_terrain_set cw_terrain_set;

headers.summary:
Triggers: data-driven "when X then Y" rules stored in scenes (the tier-3
layer of SUBSYSTEMS 8.3 that needs no script VM). A Trigger is a node:

  [node name="OnGoal" type="Trigger" parent="Goal"]
  signal = "body_entered"
  filter_group = "player"
  action = SET
  target = "../Lamp"
  member = "color"
  value = "color(0.2, 1, 0.3, 1)"

reads "when Goal emits body_entered with a node of group player, set
Lamp.color". Being a node, a trigger round-trips through .cwscene text,
shows in the editor's scene tree and inspector, undoes like any edit and
is readable and writable as plain text.

Semantics (deliberately small):
  - source (default "..", the trigger's parent): the node whose `signal`
    fires the rule. Paths are relative to the Trigger node ("..",
    "../Lamp", "/root/Level/Door", "%Unique").
  - The rule connects when the trigger becomes ready (its source is
    resolved then; a missing source or a signal the source's type does not
    declare is a warning naming the fix) and disconnects when it leaves the
    tree. Changing source/signal/enabled at runtime reconnects.
  - Firing is DEFERRED: actions run at the end of the phase that emitted
    the signal, in emission order, so a rule may free, spawn or change the
    scene safely from a physics callback.
  - filter_group: fire only when the signal's first argument is a node in
    that group (body_entered from the player, not from a crate). Empty =
    always.
  - once: fire at most once per trigger life (a pickup, a cutscene).
  - enabled: false = never fire (another trigger may SET it true).
  - Several triggers on one signal fire in tree order; one trigger does one
    action (chain more by adding triggers, or EMIT a signal another trigger
    listens to).
  - Actions (member and value are text; target defaults to ".."):
      SET           target.member = value (parsed for the property: enums
                    by name, "color(1, 0, 0, 1)", vec2(...), 3.5, true, text)
      CALL          the method `member` of target (cw_node_type_add_method or
                    the method resolver); with value empty the signal's
                    arguments are passed, else value parsed as the method's
                    first argument type
      EMIT          target emits signal `member` with the signal's arguments
      SPAWN         instance the scene file `value` as a child of target
                    (member, when set, names the new node)
      FREE          free target (and its subtree)
      CHANGE_SCENE  the scene app's main scene becomes `value`
  - fired (read-only, not saved): how many times the rule ran; the debug
    channel reads it (`get <trigger> fired`).
Anything per entity or per frame belongs in C (tier 1/2): triggers are for
the handful of "when this happens, do that" rules a human tweaks.

functions.name: cw_trigger_fire
functions.signature: bool cw_trigger_fire(cw_node trigger, const cw_value *args, int argc)
functions.doc:
Run a Trigger node's action now as if its signal fired with args (the
filter, once and enabled rules apply). false when it did not run (or the
action failed; the log says why). The editor's "test fire" uses it.

headers.summary:
cartwheel UI: a retained widget system built from scene NODES, for games
and for the editor (which is built with it).

Every widget is a node type extending Control (Control extends Node), so
controls live in the scene tree, load from .cwscene files, have reflected
properties (cw_node_set / cw_node_get_prop), emit signals (cw_connect) and
are freed with their subtree. They draw through the 2D renderer
(render2d.h) on their own canvas layer above the game.

── Rects ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Units are UI units: canvas pixels divided by the UI scale (cw_ui_set_scale;
1 by default, 2 for a pixel-art game's chunky UI, the display's density
for HiDPI). A control's rect is relative to its parent control (or to the
canvas for a top-level control, one whose parent is not a Control).
The canvas is the WINDOW, not a CanvasSettings virtual canvas: Node2Ds
use virtual pixels, controls do not (scene2d.h, "two coordinate
spaces"), unless the UI is drawn into a virtual pass with cw_ui_draw.

  - Under a plain Control (or the canvas) a child's rect comes from its
    ANCHORS (0..1 of the parent's size, per side) plus OFFSETS (UI units,
    per side), Godot-style: left = anchor_left * parent_w + offset_left,
    right = anchor_right * parent_w + offset_right. If that is smaller than
    the minimum size the rect grows (grow_horizontal / grow_vertical say
    which way).
  - Under a Container the container places children; their anchors and
    offsets are ignored. Size flags say what a child does with the space
    it gets: FILL (take the cross size), EXPAND (share the extra main-axis
    space by stretch ratio), SHRINK_CENTER / SHRINK_END (sit at min size,
    centred or at the end; neither = at the start).

── Layout ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Two passes. MEASURE: every control's minimum size is max(custom minimum
size, content minimum size), where content comes from text and theme
(a Button: its text + its style's content margins; a VBox: its children
plus separations). Sizes always derive from content and theme; nothing is
a hard-coded pixel constant. ARRANGE: top-down, each container fits its
children. Both are cached: changing a property that affects size marks the
control and its ancestors dirty, and only dirty subtrees are measured and
re-arranged (a subtree whose size did not change and is clean is moved,
not re-laid out). Container positions and sizes are rounded to whole UI
units, so layouts are exact on every host. Layout runs once per frame
before input routing and again before drawing if something changed;
cw_ui_layout forces it.

── Localization ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Text a control shows (Label/RichTextLabel/Button text, tooltips,
OptionButton/ItemList/PopupMenu items, MenuBar and TabContainer titles,
LineEdit placeholders, dialog texts) goes through cw_tr_auto when the
control's auto_translate is on (the default): text that is a catalog key
shows its translation, other text shows as written. Changing the locale
re-measures every control. Right to left (layout_direction, resolved
through the ancestors to the locale): containers and anchors mirror their
children horizontally (HBox order, Grid columns, Margin sides, anchored
rects), LEFT/RIGHT text alignments swap, check boxes and option arrows
move to the other side, and text is shaped as an RTL paragraph. Scroll
containers, split containers, tab bars, trees, sliders, progress bars and
text fields keep their left-to-right internals.

── Accessibility ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Every focusable control is reachable by Tab / Shift+Tab, the arrow keys
and the gamepad (ui_* actions); closing a popup gives focus back to the
control that had it when it opened (an OptionButton after a choice), so
keyboard and gamepad users keep their place. cw_ui_set_text_scale,
cw_ui_set_reduced_motion and the high-contrast / colorblind themes are
below; the accessibility tree, captions and remapping are in
cartwheel/a11y.h. Controls carry accessibility_name /
accessibility_description for what text alone does not say.

── Input routing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Once per frame (the platform calls the UI right after the input module,
BEFORE any fixed tick), the UI reads the raw input snapshot and routes:
  - pointer (mouse; a touch acts as the mouse): open popups first, then
    the topmost control under the pointer in reverse draw order whose
    mouse_filter is not IGNORE. Unhandled events bubble to the parent
    while the filter is PASS; STOP ends there. A press captures the
    pointer: moves and the release go to the pressed control until every
    button is up (drags). Inside a ScrollContainer a touch that moves
    past a few units becomes a scroll drag and the pressed control gets a
    canceled release.
  - keys and text: to the focus owner; unhandled Tab / Shift+Tab move
    focus in tree order, arrows / Enter / Space / Escape act as
    navigation.
  - gamepad: actions ui_up, ui_down, ui_left, ui_right, ui_accept and
    ui_cancel (cartwheel/input.h). The UI creates them with pad bindings
    (d-pad, left stick, south, east) unless the game defined them; the
    keyboard reaches navigation through the key path, so do not bind keys
    to ui_* actions. Navigation goes to the explicit focus neighbour, or
    else the nearest focusable control in that direction (geometry).
  - whatever the UI did not take is the game's: cw_ui_wants_pointer() /
    cw_ui_wants_keyboard() say whether to ignore the pointer/keys this
    frame, and an unhandled-input callback sees what fell through.
Text arrives as CW_EVENT_TEXT; the UI starts platform text input while a
text field has focus (cw_text_input_start).

── Signals (cw_connect(node, "pressed", ...)) ───────────────────────
Control: focus_entered, focus_exited, mouse_entered, mouse_exited, resized.
Buttons: pressed, toggled(bool). Range widgets: value_changed(float).
LineEdit: text_changed(string), text_submitted(string). TextEdit:
text_changed. ItemList / OptionButton / Tree: item_selected(int),
item_activated(int). Tree: item_collapsed(int, bool), multi_selected(int,
bool). PopupMenu / MenuBar:
id_pressed(int). TabContainer: tab_changed(int). RichTextLabel:
meta_clicked(string). Dialogs: confirmed, canceled. ColorPicker:
color_changed(color). Split: dragged(float). ScrollContainer:
scroll_changed.

── Drawing and cost ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
cw_ui_render draws every visible control of a tree in tree order (popups,
then tooltips on top) in its own 2D pass on the window, no clear, on canvas
layer cw_ui_layer() (default CW_R2D_MAX_LAYERS - 1). Styles (rounded
rects, borders, shadows, all anti-aliased) are vertex-coloured triangles
and text is SDF, so they batch together: a typical screen is a handful of
draw calls; clip_contents (scroll areas, text fields) costs a batch break
each. Drawing is O(visible controls); layout is O(dirty controls).

Threads: main thread only. Memory: CW_MEM_UI.

functions.name: cw_scroll_set
functions.doc:
── Containers (node types) ───────────────────────────────────────────
Container: base type, fits children to its rect.
HBoxContainer / VBoxContainer: a row / column; theme constant
  "separation"; property `alignment` (0 begin 1 center 2 end) for the
  leftover space when no child expands.
GridContainer: `columns`; constants "h_separation", "v_separation". A
  column (row) expands when any child in it has EXPAND.
MarginContainer: constants "margin_left/top/right/bottom".
CenterContainer: children at their minimum size, centred.
Panel: draws style "panel"; children placed by anchors.
PanelContainer: style "panel", children fit inside its content margins.
ScrollContainer: one content child at its minimum size (stretched to fill
  when smaller), scrolled by wheel, scrollbar drag, touch drag, and
  keyboard focus moving inside (ensure-visible). Properties
  `horizontal_scroll_mode` / `vertical_scroll_mode` (0 disabled, 1 auto,
  2 always), `scroll_horizontal` / `scroll_vertical`.
HSplitContainer / VSplitContainer: two children with a draggable
  separator; `split_offset`, `collapsed`; constant "separation".
TabContainer: one page per child (tab title = child name, or its
  its line of the `tab_titles` property, one title per line, set
  directly or through cw_tab_container_set_title); `current_tab`;
  `drag_to_rearrange`: dragging a tab starts a UI drag of kind "tab"
  (see drag and drop below) that drop targets (another TabContainer, a
  dock) accept or refuse; the container itself moves nothing.
HFlowContainer / VFlowContainer: children wrap into lines.
AspectRatioContainer: `ratio`, `stretch_mode` (0 width controls height,
  1 height controls width, 2 fit, 3 cover), `alignment_horizontal`,
  `alignment_vertical` (0 begin 1 center 2 end).

functions.name: cw_label_set_text
functions.doc:
── Widgets (node types) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
Label: `text`, `horizontal_alignment` (cw_halign), `vertical_alignment`
  (cw_valign), `autowrap` (wrap at the width; min width 0), `clip_text`,
  `ellipsis` (cut with "..." to the width), `uppercase`. Theme:
  font, font_size, font_color.
RichTextLabel: `text` with BBCode [b] [i] [color=#rrggbb] [color=name]
  [size=N] [url=meta]...[/url]; `fit_content` (min height = text). Bold
  and italic use the theme fonts "bold_font" / "italics_font" when set,
  else synthetic (double-struck / sheared). Clicking a [url] emits
  meta_clicked(meta).
Button: `text`, `disabled`, `toggle_mode`, `button_pressed`,
  `button_group` (name: toggle buttons sharing a group in one tree are
  exclusive), `alignment`, `flat`. Styles normal / hover / pressed /
  disabled / focus; colors font_color, font_hover_color,
  font_pressed_color, font_disabled_color.
CheckBox / CheckButton: toggle buttons drawn as a box / a switch.
OptionButton: a button with a popup list; `items` ("A\nB\nC"),
  `selected`; emits item_selected.
HSlider / VSlider / SpinBox / ProgressBar extend Range: `min_value`,
  `max_value`, `step` (0 = continuous), `value`, `page` (the value
  stops at max_value - page, as in Godot: a scrollbar thumb of size page
  ends at max_value). SpinBox: arrows,
  typed numbers, `suffix`, `prefix`. ProgressBar: `show_percentage`.
LineEdit: `text`, `placeholder_text`, `max_length` (characters, 0 = no
  limit), `secret` (draws `secret_character`), `editable`; caret +
  selection (mouse drag, double-click word, shift+arrows/home/end, ctrl+a),
  clipboard (ctrl+c/x/v), undo (ctrl+z).
TextEdit: `text`, `editable`, `show_line_numbers`, `highlight_current_line`;
  long lines scroll horizontally (no wrapping); multi-line caret and selection, scrolling, clipboard, a
  syntax highlighter hook (cw_text_edit_set_highlighter; cw_ui_highlight_c
  is a ready one for C).
ItemList: items with optional icons, `select_mode` (0 single 1 multi),
  `items` text; scrolling.
Tree: rows of items with columns, expand/collapse, selection; `columns`,
  `hide_root`, `items` (indented text: two spaces per level, '|' between
  columns) for scene files; the C API below for code. `select_mode` 1 =
  multiple selection: ctrl+click toggles a row, shift+click selects the
  range from the last clicked row, a plain click selects one row (on
  release when it was already selected, so a selection can be dragged);
  every membership change emits multi_selected(item, selected) and the
  focused row still emits item_selected. `drag_items`: pressing a row
  and moving starts a UI drag of kind "tree_item" (payload = the item's
  metadata, text = its first column, label "N items" for a multi drag);
  make the tree (or anything) a drop target and place the drop with
  cw_uitree_item_at's section (above / on / below a row).
PopupMenu: items (label, id, check, separator, submenu = child PopupMenu
  name); `items` text: "Open|1\n-\nRecent>RecentMenu\n[x]Grid|7".
  cw_popup_menu_popup shows it at a point; emits id_pressed(id). An item
  may show shortcut text at its right (cw_popup_menu_set_shortcut; theme
  color font_shortcut_color); the menu only draws it, the app binds keys.
PopupPanel: a Popup that draws style "panel" and fits its children inside
  the panel's content margins (command palettes, quick pickers);
  cw_popup_show places and opens it (any Popup, in fact).
MenuBar: one title per child PopupMenu (its `title`, else its name).
AcceptDialog / ConfirmationDialog: `title`, `dialog_text`, `ok_text`,
  `cancel_text`; modal; cw_dialog_popup_centered; confirmed / canceled.
ColorPicker: `color`; HSV square + hue strip + alpha strip + hex readout.
TextureRect: `texture` (asset path) or cw_texture_rect_set_texture;
  `stretch_mode` (0 scale, 1 tile, 2 keep, 3 keep centered, 4 keep aspect,
  5 keep aspect centered, 6 keep aspect covered); `region_rect`; `filter`
  (LINEAR | NEAREST for pixel art). Path textures load once per path and
  filter, shared with the 2D nodes (Sprite2D ...).
NinePatchRect: `texture`, `patch_margin_left/top/right/bottom`,
  `draw_center`, `filter`.
CaptionPanel: the active captions and subtitles (cartwheel/a11y.h), one
  box per line, newest at the bottom; theme "CaptionPanel": panel,
  font, font_size, font_color, speaker_color, separation.
RemapButton: a Button showing an input action's binding (`action`,
  `slot`, `device` KEYBOARD_MOUSE | GAMEPAD); pressing it captures the
  next key/button/axis as the new binding; emits remapped(binding).

headers.summary:
cartwheel 3D vehicles: a wheeled body on Box3D (physics3d.h) with
raycast suspension and a friction-circle tyre model. Cars, karts, trucks,
buggies, an arcade car-ball that drives up walls.

The chassis is an ordinary dynamic cw_body3d you make (its shapes give it
mass, inertia and its crashes); the wheels are not bodies. Each tick,
before cw_world3d_step, cw_vehicle3d_update casts one ray per wheel from
its anchor along the chassis's LOCAL down (so a car on a wall or a ceiling
still stands on its wheels there), and where a wheel touches it applies
impulses to the chassis (and the reaction to the ground, when the ground
is a dynamic body: a car riding up on another pushes it down):

  suspension  a spring and damper along the suspension axis, from the
              wheel's hertz and damping ratio and its share of the sprung
              mass, never pulling; a bump stop at full compression
  tyre        drive, brake and sideways grip at the contact share one
              friction circle of radius grip * load: inside it the tyre
              holds (lateral_stiffness of the sideways skid cancelled per
              tick: 1 = rails), past it the tyre slides, and a sliding
              tyre keeps slide_grip of its grip until it slows back
              inside the circle, so a car carves at low speed and drifts
              when pushed
  ploughing   (plough_grip, off by default) a wheel sliding sideways
              faster than plough_speed digs into loose ground and grips
              harder, at the contact: what trips and rolls a car shoved
              sideways on dirt (roll_influence 1)
  handbrake   drops the grip of the wheels marked handbrake to
              handbrake_grip and (handbrake_locks) locks them: the rear
              swings round
  resistance  rolling resistance while a wheel touches, air drag always

Steering, drive and brake are set per axle (a wheel names its axle):
cw_vehicle3d_set_axle. Everything the game might read is a plain field of
cw_vehicle3d / cw_wheel3d (contact, normal, compression, load, slip, spin).
The wheels' render transforms interpolate like bodies do.

Frame of the chassis (local): up (0, 1, 0), forward (0, 0, 1) by default;
left is up x forward. A positive steer angle turns a wheel's front toward
the left (counter-clockwise seen from above); a positive spin rolls it
forward.

Typical tick:
  init:          chassis = cw_body3d_create(...) + shapes; cw_vehicle3d_init(&car, chassis, &def)
  fixed_update:  cw_vehicle3d_set_axle(&car, 0, steer, 0, brake);
                 cw_vehicle3d_set_axle(&car, 1, 0, drive, brake);
                 cw_vehicle3d_update(&car, dt); cw_world3d_step(w, dt);
  render:        cw_world3d_sync(w, alpha); wheel i at cw_vehicle3d_wheel_world(&car, i, alpha)

Determinism: only + - * / sqrt and cartwheel/math.h, sorted world queries,
wheels in index order: the same inputs give the same bits on every host
and with any number of step workers (cw_world3d_def.workers, 0 = all).
Threads: main thread, outside the step, like the rest of physics3d.h.
A cw_vehicle3d is a plain struct owned by the caller (no allocation); it
holds the chassis handle but does not own the body.

types.name: cw_wheel3d_def
types.decl:
typedef struct cw_wheel3d_def {
  t3_vec3 anchor;          /* chassis-local wheel centre at FULL compression (the top of its travel) */
  int axle;                /* 0..CW_VEHICLE3D_AXLES-1: 0 */
  float radius;            /* m: 0.35 */
  float travel;            /* m of suspension, full compression to full droop: 0.25 */
  float hertz;             /* suspension frequency with its share of the mass: 1.6 */
  float damping_ratio;     /* 0.5 */
  float grip;              /* friction coefficient of the tyre (the ground's material is not used): 1 */
  float slide_grip;        /* share of grip left while the tyre slides: 0.85 */
  float lateral_stiffness; /* share of the sideways skid cancelled per tick inside the circle, 0..1: 1 */
  float plough_grip;       /* loose ground: extra friction a wheel builds sliding sideways, as it digs a
                              furrow (soil tripping, what rolls a car shoved sideways on dirt): 0 = off */
  float plough_speed;      /* m/s of sideways slide where ploughing starts; full grip at twice it: 6 */
  bool handbrake;          /* the handbrake acts on this wheel */
  bool handbrake_locks;    /* it locks the wheel (stops its roll: a skid); false = it only lowers the
                              grip (a powerslide with the drive still on): true */
  float handbrake_grip;    /* share of grip under the handbrake: 0.35 */
} cw_wheel3d_def;

headers.summary:
Project files: a writable view of a project for the editor and tools.

Reads look in the writable layer first, then fall through to the app's
read-only assets (cw_asset_*). Writes:
  - natively, with a project directory set (cw_vfs_set_root or CW_PROJECT),
    go straight to disk;
  - in a cart (carts cannot write files: wasmcart has no write path), stay
    in memory, and the whole set of changes moves as ONE archive blob:
    cw_vfs_export / cw_vfs_import, reachable through the debug channel
    (`vfs export` / `vfs import <base64>`) so romdev or a companion
    process can carry a project in and out with no new ABI. (A host
    "project directory" capability would be an ABI addition.)

Layers, top first: the in-memory layer (every write lands here too, so a
native write is read back without touching the disk), the project
directory on disk (native, when a root is set), then the assets (natively
the mounted .cwpak and the loose asset root, in a cart its bundle). A file
removed while a lower, read-only layer still has it (a cart's bundle, an
asset root that is not the project) is hidden by a REMOVAL mark in the
memory layer: it reads as missing, lists as absent and exports as a
removal, so the change travels with the archive.

Paths are relative, '/'-separated, no "..".

headers.summary:
cartwheel video: MPEG-1 playback for cutscenes (pl_mpeg).

A cw_video plays an MPEG-1 program stream (.mpg: MPEG-1 video, MP2
audio). Make one with ffmpeg, e.g.
  ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v mpeg1video -q:v 4 -c:a mp2 -b:a 128k -f mpeg out.mpg

── Time ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The game says which moment to show: cw_video_update(v, t) with t in
seconds since the video started, taken from the fixed tick count (e.g.
(cw_tick_index() - start_tick) * cw_fixed_dt()), never from a clock. The
frame shown is floor(t * fps), so a replay, a slow machine and every host
show the same frame on the same tick. Decoding moves forward frame by
frame; a t earlier than the current frame (or a loop) restarts from the
beginning. MPEG-1 decoding is integer, so frames are identical everywhere.

── Picture ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cw_video_texture returns a render target (cartwheel/render2d.h) holding
the current frame as RGB: draw it as a sprite (cw_r2d_sprite), GL or
WebGPU alike. The decoder produces Y, Cb and Cr planes; they are uploaded
and converted to RGB by a shader on the GPU, only when a new frame was
decoded and only when the texture is asked for, so call cw_video_texture
where you draw (render), not in update. On GL a conversion changes GL
state the way a 2D pass does (cartwheel/render2d.h): call it before your
2D pass, or reset three.c's bindings after it (t3_renderer_reset_bindings).

── Sound ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A file with audio plays it as a stream voice (cartwheel/audio.h) started
by the first cw_video_update, on the bus and volume of the desc (needs
cw_audio_init). Its MP2 frames are decoded on the audio job pool like
any stream. The audio runs on the mixer's clock: over a long video it may
drift from the tick clock by the difference between the two (a few ms a
minute), which a cutscene does not notice.

Cost: decoding is on the game thread, in cw_video_update: about 0.22 ms
per 320x180 frame on a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 core (about 0.9 ms at 640x360);
the GPU conversion is one triangle over the target.

functions.name: cw_video_open
functions.doc:
Opens a video from the asset bundle (the file is read into memory and
kept; the first frame is decoded here, nothing else). Logs and returns the null handle
when the asset is missing or not an MPEG-1 program stream. Main thread.

functions.name: cw_video_close
functions.doc: Stops its audio voice and frees everything. Stale handle: no-op.

functions.name: cw_video_update
functions.doc:
Shows the frame for t seconds since the start (see Time). Returns the
frame index now shown (the last one once a non-looping video has ended),
-1 for a stale handle.

functions.name: cw_video_texture
functions.doc:
The current frame as an RGB render target, converted on the GPU if a new
frame was decoded since the last call (see Picture). Owned by the video.

functions.name: cw_video_get_info
functions.doc: false for a stale handle

functions.name: cw_video_ended
functions.doc: A non-looping video's t has reached its end.

functions.name: cw_video_voice
functions.doc: The audio voice (the null handle without sound or before the first update).

functions.name: cw_video_frame_hash
functions.doc:
FNV-1a over the current frame's Y, Cb and Cr planes (what the decoder
produced, before the GPU): what the cross-host tests compare.

types.name: cw_video_desc
cw_video_info

headers.summary:
Visibility: culling, LOD and impostors for the tree's 3D meshes.

A tree opts in with a VisibilityManager node (the first one in tree order
counts); without one, three.c's own per-object frustum test is all there
is. Everything below works on MeshInstance3D nodes.

── node types (properties: docs/nodes.json) ────────────────────────────
  VisibilityManager  (Node) the switches and the read-only statistics:
    frustum_cull      BVH over static meshes (O(visible): a BVH4 walked
                      four child boxes at a time with SIMD, its top levels
                      spread over the job pool) plus a flat SIMD pass over
                      moving ones
    occlusion_cull    GPU occlusion queries (ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED_CONSERVATIVE)
                      on each candidate's bounding box against the depth the
                      scene just drew; results are read a frame later, so a
                      frame draws the PREVIOUS frame's visible set. Boxes are
                      inflated by occlusion_margin plus the camera's motion
                      over the query latency, objects new to the frustum
                      start visible, and a result that is late more than
                      two frames counts as visible: disocclusion is seen
                      before the object is, so nothing pops in. Visible
                      objects are re-queried every occlusion_interval frames
                      (staggered), occluded ones every frame.
                      occlusion_wait reads each result as soon as the next
                      frame starts, waiting for it if the GPU is behind (the
                      same counts on every host: tests)
    occlusion_guard   (true) what keeps queries from popping a moving
                      camera: boxes also grow by tan(6 x turn + 6 x step /
                      distance to the nearest drawn static box) per metre
                      of distance, a box the grown query would clip or
                      straddle the frustum edge with is treated as
                      visible, and while the camera is closer to a drawn
                      static box than occlusion_margin + 3 x its step this
                      frame no result is trusted and NO queries are
                      issued. So a fast camera brushing past props skips
                      occlusion culling altogether: vis_city's street run
                      (up to 0.9 m a frame, 0.6 m from the street trees)
                      issues no queries from about tick 10 to 220, and
                      its occlusion counts only appear once the camera
                      slows. Off: plain one-frame-late queries, which pop.
    portals           Room3D / Portal3D culling (below), when rooms exist
    lod               pick each mesh's LOD: mesh resources and glTF scenes
                      use their cwpack LOD chains (the coarsest level whose
                      simplification error stays within lod_error_px pixels
                      on screen); SPHERE and CYLINDER primitives have
                      built-in coarser tessellations picked the same way
    lod_error_px      the screen-space error budget (1 pixel)
    impostors         far meshes with `impostor` set draw as octahedral
                      impostors (below)
    shadow_distance   how far a shadow caster's box is swept along the
                      light when frustum culling (a caster outside the view
                      still shadows what is inside); casters are never
                      occlusion or portal culled while a DirectionalLight3D
                      casts shadows; with an omni or spot light casting
                      shadows, casters are not culled at all
    stats (read-only) meshes, static_meshes, visible, frustum_culled,
                      occlusion_culled, portal_culled, distance_culled,
                      queries (issued last frame), query_latency (frames
                      the last result took), lod_counts (vec4: meshes drawn
                      at LOD 0, 1, 2, 3 and coarser), impostors (drawn),
                      impostor_fading (drawn with their mesh, crossfading),
                      bvh_nodes, rooms_visible, cull_ms (CPU)
  MeshInstance3D gains:
    static            the mesh does not move: it joins the BVH (moving it
                      later is allowed; the BVH is refitted)
    lod_bias          scales the error budget for this mesh (2 = coarser)
    visibility_range  hidden beyond this distance (0 = no limit)
    occlusion_cull    may be hidden by occlusion queries (true)
    impostor          beyond impostor_distance the mesh draws as an
                      impostor: its look from 64 directions (an 8x8
                      octahedral grid) baked into an atlas the first time
                      it is needed, lit by the tree's directional, ambient
                      and hemisphere lights; instances with the same
                      geometry, materials and scale share one atlas. Over
                      impostor_fade metres the impostor fades in over the
                      still-drawn mesh (which goes only once the impostor
                      is opaque), so the switch never pops
    lod (read-only)   the level drawn last frame (-1 culled, 100 impostor)
  Room3D             (Node3D) a box (extents = half sizes) of interior
                     space; static meshes whose box centre is inside belong
                     to it
  Portal3D           (Node3D) a size.x by size.y opening in the node's XY
                     plane joining the rooms on its two sides (no room on a
                     side = the outside); enabled = false closes it (a shut
                     door). From a room, the camera sees other rooms only
                     through portals, each narrowing the view to the
                     portal's screen rectangle; from outside, rooms are seen
                     through their portals to the outside.

Where it runs: the pipeline's "visibility" SHADOW-phase pass (order 2000,
after engine shadow maps, which so still see every caster)
culls, picks LODs and bakes impostors before the scene draws; culled meshes
are hidden for the frame and shown again by the "visibility_restore"
PRESENT pass, so game code never sees the flags change. "impostors" (OPAQUE,
100) draws the impostors; "occlusion_queries" (OPAQUE, 900) issues the
queries against the finished depth.

Costs per frame: the BVH walk (visible boxes plus their near misses), a
pass over moving meshes, a pass over visible meshes for LOD, one query
draw per queried mesh, one instanced draw per impostor atlas. The first use
of an impostor atlas renders the mesh 128 times (64 views, albedo and
normals). GL and WebGPU bake the same atlas and draw the same impostors.

functions.name: cw_visibility_get_stats
functions.doc: The last frame's numbers (zero without a VisibilityManager).

functions.name: cw_visibility_drawn
functions.doc:
Whether the visibility pass drew this MeshInstance3D last frame (as a mesh
or an impostor).

types.name: cw_visibility_stats

headers.summary:
Water: a wavy surface that reflects, refracts and flows, and things that
float on it. A port of three.js r187's Water / Water2 / WaterMesh add-ons
(planar reflection and refraction rendered from mirrored and clipped
cameras, scrolling normal maps, flow maps) with Gerstner waves (GPU Gems
1, chapter 1) moving the surface itself.

── node types ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Water3D      (Node3D) a rectangle of water of `size` (x by z metres)
               in the node's XZ plane, its rest level at the node's y,
               facing +Y. Properties:
    size, subdivisions   the grid the waves move (quads along the longer
                         side; quality scales it: Low 1/4, Medium 1/2)
    wave_count, wave0..wave3   up to four Gerstner waves, each a vec4:
                         direction (degrees, 0 = +X, 90 = +Z), wavelength
                         (m), amplitude (m), steepness (0..1: 0 round
                         swells, 1 sharp crests; the waves' steepness is
                         shared so crests never loop over)
    wave_speed, time_offset   multiplies deep-water speed (sqrt(g / k));
                         seconds added to the waves' clock
    color                tint of what is seen through the water (linear)
    deep_color           the water body's colour where no refraction is
                         drawn (Low, Medium)
    murk                 share of the refraction lost into deep_color
                         (0.7; 0 = clear as glass)
    detail, roughness    the normal map ripples' strength; the surface
                         roughness the lights' glints see
    reflectivity         Fresnel F0 (0.02, water)
    distortion           how far the normal maps bend reflection and
                         refraction
    normal_map           a tangent-space normal map image (empty: a
                         seamless gen://noise normal map), scrolled twice
                         along the flow (Water2's two-phase flow)
    normal_scale         normal map repeats per metre
    flow_direction       vec2, the flow without a flow map
    flow_speed           how fast the normal maps scroll (Water2's 0.03)
    flow_map             optional image: RG = the flow direction at each
                         point (Water2's flowMap, 0.5 = still), over the
                         whole rectangle
    reflection, refraction   draw them (quality may turn them down or off)
    resolution_scale     of the reflection and refraction targets (0.5)
    debug_view           NONE, or HEIGHT: the surface's height as colour
                         (tests read it back: R, G = height's 16 bits
                         over debug_range, B = 1)
    debug_range          vec2 (min, max) heights for debug_view HEIGHT

    floor_map_size       cells along the longer side of the baked floor depth
                         map (128; 0 = no map, no shore shading). The map is
                         made once, from the tree's static physics shapes: a
                         static shape holding the point at the rest level is
                         land (depth 0); else the highest static hit of a ray
                         down from the rest level is the floor, a miss is deep
    floor_range          metres under the rest level the rays probe (40)
    shallow_color        colour of the water over a shallow floor (linear);
                         it blends to deep_color as the depth grows
    clarity              metres of water over which the shallow colour has
                         become deep_color (5)
    shore_foam           width in metres of the foam where the water meets
                         the floor (0.7; 0 = none)
    crest_foam           0..1: foam on the wave crests where the surface
                         bunches up (0.35; 0 = none)

    scatter, glint       the turquoise light the sun sends through crests
                         toward the eye (needs a ProceduralSky); the fine
                         sparkle of the sun on small ripples
    ripple_cells, ripple_size, ripple_center, ripple_speed, ripple_damping,
    ripple_strength, foam_fade, rain, rain_size, rain_strength, splash_fx,
    splash_fx_min        the interactive ripple layer (see cw_water_splash)

  Buoyancy3D   (Node3D) child of a RigidBody3D: pushes it up where its
               probes are under the water and drags it where they are
               wet. Properties:
    water                the Water3D (empty = the tree's first)
    probes               "x y z, x y z, ..." in the body's space (empty:
                         the eight corners of its first BOX shape, or a
                         sphere's / capsule's bounding box, at 90%)
    volume               m^3 the body displaces when fully under (0: the
                         box's volume); shared out equally over probes
    probe_depth          metres over which a probe goes from dry to fully
                         under (0: a quarter of the box's height)
    fluid_density        1000 (kg/m^3)
    linear_drag          N per m/s per fully wet probe, against the probe
                         point's velocity relative to the water's
    angular_drag         N*m per rad/s, scaled by the wet share
    splash, wake         how much of a splash entering the water and of a
                         wake moving through it the body makes (1; 0: none)
    submerged            read-only: the wet share of the probes, 0..1

── time and determinism ────────────────────────────────────────────────
The waves run on the tree's fixed clock: their time is cw_tree_tick x the
fixed dt (plus time_offset), never a wall clock. Every wave phase is
reduced into [0, 2 pi) in double precision (fmod is exact) and the sums
use cw_sin / cw_cos, so cw_water_height_at and Buoyancy3D are the same
bits on every host. The GPU evaluates the same sums from the same reduced
phases (native sin / cos, so to float rounding) at the grid's vertices;
between vertices the drawn surface is flat, so it is within the grid's
sag of cw_water_height_at (a few millimetres at the default grid).

Drawing renders the scene twice more before the main pass, as r187's
Reflector and Refractor do: mirrored about the rest level (an oblique
near plane clips what is below it) and clipped to below it, each at
resolution_scale, with the water hidden (Low draws neither: the
environment's specular stands in for the reflection, deep_color for the
refraction; Medium draws the reflection only). Costs: the water guide;
on the 890M the water_boat frame is 1.0 ms (Low) to 2.1 ms (Ultra) of GPU
time on GL at 1080p, a height query 0.25 us on the CPU.

functions.name: cw_waves_displace
functions.signature: void cw_waves_displace(const cw_waves *w, float x0, float z0, double t, float out[3], float out_normal[3])
functions.doc:
Where the surface point that rests at (x0, z0) is at time t: out[0..2] =
its displaced local position (x, height, z). out_normal (may be NULL):
the surface's unit normal there. Deterministic (cw_sin / cw_cos, phases
reduced in double).

functions.name: cw_waves_height
functions.signature: float cw_waves_height(const cw_waves *w, float x, float z, double t)
functions.doc:
The surface's height above the rest level over the local point (x, z) at
time t. Gerstner waves move points sideways too, so this finds the rest
point that lands on (x, z) first (four fixed-point steps, converged to
well under a millimetre for steepness below 1). Deterministic.

functions.name: cw_water_find
functions.doc: The tree's first Water3D (null when it has none). O(1) after the first call per tree.

functions.name: cw_water_time
functions.doc:
The time the waves of a Water3D are at now, in seconds: its tree's fixed
ticks x the fixed dt + time_offset. 0 for a null node.

functions.name: cw_water_height_at
functions.signature: float cw_water_height_at(cw_node water, float x, float z, double t)
functions.doc:
The surface's world height over world (x, z) at time t (cw_water_time
for now). Outside the rectangle the waves continue (open sea). The rest
level when water is not a Water3D. Deterministic.

functions.name: cw_water_sample_at
functions.signature: bool cw_water_sample_at(cw_node water, float x, float z, double t, cw_water_sample *out)
functions.doc:
Height, normal and water velocity at world (x, z), time t. False (out
zeroed but for a flat normal) when water is not a Water3D. Deterministic.

functions.name: cw_water_get_waves
functions.doc: The Water3D's waves, as cw_waves (for cw_waves_* in its local space).

functions.name: cw_water_floor_depth_at
functions.signature: float cw_water_floor_depth_at(cw_node water, float x, float z)
functions.doc:
The water's baked floor: metres of water over the floor at world (x, z)
at rest (0 where the floor is land or above the rest level; a large value
where the map has no floor or the point is outside it). Deterministic: it
comes from physics ray casts, never from the GPU. 1e6 for a null or
unbaked water.

functions.name: cw_water_rebake_floor
functions.doc:
Bake the floor map again (the static shapes changed). Done on the next
frame.

functions.name: cw_water_splash
functions.signature: void cw_water_splash(cw_node water, float x, float z, float radius, float depth, float foam)
functions.doc:
A round dent of "depth" metres at the centre and "radius" metres wide at
world (x, z), with "foam" (0..1) left on it; it spreads out as a ring. A
deep enough one (splash_fx_min) also restarts the next particle emitter of
the splash_fx pool at the surface. No-op without a ripple grid.

functions.name: cw_water_wake
functions.signature: void cw_water_wake(cw_node water, float x, float z, float vx, float vz, float radius, float depth, float foam)
functions.doc:
A body moving through the water at (vx, vz): call once per fixed tick; it
leaves a trough and foam along its path.

functions.name: cw_water_ripple_at
functions.signature: float cw_water_ripple_at(cw_node water, float x, float z)
functions.doc: The ripple height in metres over world (x, z) (0 outside the grid).

functions.name: cw_water_ripple_hash
functions.doc: A hash of the ripple field (heights and foam): the cross-host test. 0 without a grid.

functions.name: cw_water_get_stats
functions.doc: Zeroed when t is NULL or has no water.

types.name: cw_water_wave
types.doc: One Gerstner wave (what Water3D's wave0..wave3 hold).

types.name: cw_waves
types.doc:
A set of waves, the pure-function form of a Water3D's (local space: x, z
on the rest plane, y up from the rest level).

types.name: cw_water_sample
types.doc: What the water is doing at a world point.

types.name: cw_water_stats
types.doc: Last frame's numbers for a tree's water.
